# matrix: full reference

Generated by `npm run docs` from the files below; each follows a line with its path from the package root.

<!-- Source: skills/matrix/SKILL.md -->

---
name: matrix
description: Build and review UI with matrix, wadakatu's design system (@wadakatu/matrix) for wadakatu.dev. Use when building or changing any page, component or style for wadakatu.dev or for matrix itself; when choosing colours, type, spacing or motion; when adding a component; and when reviewing UI for consistency with the system. It says where to look before writing markup, which tokens to read by role, the seven laws and the check that catches each, how to add a component, and gives one worked example.
---

# matrix

Every path here is from the package root: `node_modules/@wadakatu/matrix/` in a repository that
installs matrix, the repository itself when working on matrix. For a topic not covered below, open
[skills/matrix/references/index.md](skills/matrix/references/index.md).

## 1. Search before creating

1. Open [docs/components.json](docs/components.json). Each entry has `name`, `status`, `class`,
   `element`, `attributes`, `tokens`, `purpose`, `classes` and `doc`. Search `purpose` and
   `classes` for what you need.
2. If an entry fits, read its page (its `doc` path, for example
   [src/components/figures/figures.md](src/components/figures/figures.md)) and copy its Contract:
   the HTML with every class, attribute and ARIA it needs. Variants and states are attributes.
3. In an Astro site, use the component from `@wadakatu/matrix/astro` rather than writing the markup.
4. Only when no entry fits, compose from existing components; a new component is made in matrix
   (section 5), never in the site.

`approved` components are ported from the approved prototype: use them as they are. `draft` ones are
designed in matrix and may still change.

## 2. Tokens by role

Read every colour, type size, space, radius, layer and duration as a custom property:
`var(--mx-color-accent)` for `color.accent`. [docs/tokens.md](docs/tokens.md) lists them all with
their values in the four contexts (phosphor or operator, night or day). In TypeScript the type
`MxToken` (`dist/tokens.d.ts`) names every token. Never write a hex, a named colour, a pixel font
size or a number z-index.

| Role | Use it for |
| --- | --- |
| `color.ground` | The page; text on a filled accent face; the code block background |
| `color.panel` | The solid surface reading text sits on; hover fills |
| `color.text` | All running text |
| `color.text-lead` | Short emphasised runs: titles, `strong`, hover. Not paragraphs |
| `color.text-muted` | Meta, captions, hints. Dim text with this, never `opacity` |
| `color.accent` | Identity, links, headings, prompts, current state. Never body text; never assume green |
| `color.on-accent` | Text on an accent fill |
| `color.focus` | Focus outlines only |
| `color.control-border` | The box of a control identified by its box |
| `color.rule` | Decorative hairlines only; never a control's only boundary |
| `color.glow` | The name line and lit bits in 機械用; never reading text |
| `color.rain.tail`, `color.rain.body`, `color.rain.head` | Rain drops. Decoration, never text |
| `color.reading.human`, `color.reading.machine` | The capsule switch's dots only |
| `color.scanline` | The 機械用 scan-line wash only |

Fluid sizes are derived properties, not tokens: `--mx-text-title`, `--mx-text-entry`,
`--mx-text-prompt`, `--mx-measure`, `--mx-pad` ([src/css/foundations.md](src/css/foundations.md)).

## 3. The seven laws, and how you will be caught

| Law | Check | How you will be caught |
| --- | --- | --- |
| L1 Only real words fall | Decoration (rain, strands, decode, boot lines) is made of the site's own data; no placeholder glyphs, no invented metrics | Review. In matrix, `npm run test:specimens` checks the masthead's strip holds only the masthead's words |
| L2 Reading text never sits on rain | Text is on `color.ground` or `color.panel`; dimmed with `color.text-muted` | `npm run check` fails a role under its contrast floor or rain over its ceiling, in all four contexts; `npm run test:stories` runs axe at `error` |
| L3 Two readings, one source | 機械用 and 人間用 render the same data | Review; the specimens render both readings from one fixture |
| L4 Every effect has a still | Motion is stepped, finite and skippable; the still is what reduced motion, `?motion=0` and no JavaScript show | `npm run test:specimens`: with Hold rain on, no endless animation runs; the stills of rain, the switch and the boot are tested |
| L5 The mark is whole | The logo file as designed: no crop, radius, mask, transform or redraw | `npm run test:specimens` checks the mark is the real file, whole, and that the boot moves a cover, not the image |
| L6 One language per page | A run of the other language carries `lang` | `npm run test:specimens` checks such a run takes its own face; `npm run test:visual` checks an English page marks an article's Japanese title and headings |
| L7 Night first; roles, never hues | No hue in a name; read `color.accent`, never green | The stylelint config fails a hex, a named colour or a colour function; the drift script fails an unknown `--mx-*` property or `mx-*` class |

In a repository that uses matrix, two of these are yours to run:

- `extends: ["@wadakatu/matrix/stylelint"]` in your stylelint config
  ([stylelint/index.mjs](stylelint/index.mjs)): no raw colour, font size or z-index; only the four
  breakpoints, 600, 720, 1100 and 1360px.
- `node node_modules/@wadakatu/matrix/scripts/drift.mjs src` ([scripts/drift.mjs](scripts/drift.mjs)):
  every `--mx-*` property is a token or matrix's, and every `mx-*` class is in the index.

## 4. Page patterns

| Pattern | What it fixes | Specimen |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Machine-first landing | The site opens as the shell; four visible ways to 人間用 | `home` |
| Twin routes | 機械用 owns the short address; 人間用 is the same tree under `human/` | `human-home`, `projects`, `human-projects` |
| Single-reading document | An article has one address; its switch links into the shell at its file | `article-a`, `article-b`, `article-c` |
| Article page | Masthead, contents beside one body panel, rain as a band | `article-a`, `article-b`, `article-c`, `blog` |
| Moved address | A stub page, because GitHub Pages cannot redirect | `moved` |
| Notice page | 404 and offline: one panel, no chrome, nothing to fetch | `not-found`, `offline` |
| Language twin | English at the root, Japanese under `/ja/`, linked with `hreflang` and the language link | None; see [src/components/lang/lang.md](src/components/lang/lang.md) |

Specimens are full pages in matrix's Storybook, under Specimens; they are not in the package.

## 5. Adding a component (in matrix)

1. Search the index first (section 1). Add a component only for a need no entry meets.
2. Make `src/components/<name>/` with `<name>.css`, `mx-<name>.ts` (only if it has behaviour),
   `<Name>.astro`, `<Name>.stories.ts` and `<name>.md`.
3. The page has front matter in this order: `name`, `status`, `class`, `element` (each where there is
   one), `attributes`, `tokens`; then seven headings: Purpose, Contract, Variants and states,
   Behaviour, Tokens, Accessibility, Do / Don't. `tokens` lists exactly what its files read.
4. Run `npm run docs` (regenerates the index, `llms.txt` and `llms-full.txt`), then `npm run build`
   and `npm run check`.

Done means (04):

1. The doc has the seven headings and its contract matches the Astro component's output.
2. It reads only tokens; the no-raw-values lint passes.
3. Stories: default, every variant and state, all four contexts in one grid, Japanese, the still.
4. Accessibility checks pass at `error`; the keyboard path is in the doc.
5. It works with JavaScript disabled, or its doc says exactly what is missing.
6. Visual baselines are committed for 1440 and 390 wide (`npm run test:visual:update`, in Docker).
7. Approved components: a side-by-side still against the prototype, every difference listed.

## 6. Worked example

**Input.** "On 人間用 Projects, add a list of each project's latest commit subjects."

**Search.** `docs/components.json` has Log, whose purpose reads "A list of the repository's real
commit subjects, the material the rain is made of (L1)." It fits, so nothing is created. Its page,
[src/components/log/log.md](src/components/log/log.md), gives the contract; Panel's gives the
surface it sits on (L2).

**Output, the markup:**

```html
<section class="mx-panel" aria-labelledby="commits">
  <h2 id="commits">Latest commits</h2>
  <ol class="mx-log"><li>feat: …</li><li>fix: …</li></ol>
</section>
```

The subjects come from the site's data, filtered as the corpus is (L1); 機械用 shows the same
subjects (L3).

**Output, the tokens read:** Log's `tokens` in the index, `color.rule`, `font.size.meta`,
`space.1`, `space.4`, `border.width.hair`, and Panel's, which begin `color.panel`, `color.rule`,
`color.accent`. The site adds no CSS of its own for the list.

**Output, the stories:** none, because matrix did not change. Had Log needed a new variant, the
change would be made to Log in matrix, with its stories gaining that variant in the Contexts grid,
in Japanese and as a still, and `npm run docs` run before `npm run check`.

<!-- Source: docs/tokens.md -->

# Tokens

Generated from `tokens/` by `npm run docs`. Do not edit; `npm run check` fails when this
file differs from a fresh build. Values are the CSS values in `dist/tokens.json`.

## Colour roles

| Token | Custom property | phosphor-night | phosphor-day | operator-night | operator-day | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `color.accent` | `--mx-color-accent` | `#2bf07a` | `#0a5a31` | `#d9b56a` | `#0a4f2f` | The lit colour of the context (phosphor green or operator amber). Use for identity, links, headings, prompts, current state. Never running body text, and never assume it is green. Must clear 4.5:1 on ground and panel. |
| `color.control-border` | `--mx-color-control-border` | `#80c194` | `#2a4735` | `#c2b496` | `#2f4236` | The boundary of a control that is identified by its box. Alias of color.text-muted. Must clear 3:1 on ground and panel. |
| `color.focus` | `--mx-color-focus` | `#2bf07a` | `#0a5a31` | `#d9b56a` | `#0a4f2f` | The focus indicator. Alias of color.accent. Use only for focus outlines. Must clear 3:1 on ground and panel. |
| `color.glow` | `--mx-color-glow` | `#2bf07a73` | `#0a5a3100` | `#d9b56a73` | `#0a4f2f00` | Phosphor bloom: accent at 45% alpha at night, transparent by day, so text-shadow needs no theme selector. For the name line and lit bits in 機械用 only; never on reading text. |
| `color.ground` | `--mx-color-ground` | `#020805` | `#ccd7c9` | `#100e0b` | `#cdd6cb` | The screen itself, the darkest surface at night. Use for the page background, text on a filled accent face, and the code block background. Never a foreground on another surface. |
| `color.on-accent` | `--mx-color-on-accent` | `#020805` | `#ccd7c9` | `#100e0b` | `#cdd6cb` | Text on an accent fill (filled controls, the status line). Alias of color.ground. Must clear 4.5:1 on accent. |
| `color.panel` | `--mx-color-panel` | `#06120b` | `#dee7db` | `#17140f` | `#dbe2d9` | A solid reading surface laid on the ground. Use for panels and hover fills. Reading text sits only on ground or panel. |
| `color.rain.body` | `--mx-color-rain-body` | `#1a8f4a` | `#5f8c6c` | `#8a7b5e` | `#6f8073` | Body of a rain drop. Decoration only; never text. Has a contrast ceiling: at most 5:1 on ground, so rain stays below reading brightness (law L2). |
| `color.rain.head` | `--mx-color-rain-head` | `#d6ffe2` | `#0a3a20` | `#f0e0b4` | `#06281a` | Leading glyph of a rain drop. Decoration only; never text. |
| `color.rain.tail` | `--mx-color-rain-tail` | `#0b3d20` | `#b9c9b8` | `#2a251d` | `#b7c3b6` | Dimmest end of a rain drop. Decoration only; never text. |
| `color.reading.human` | `--mx-color-reading-human` | `#58b7ff` | `#0b5cad` | `#58b7ff` | `#0b5cad` | Dot on the 人間用 side of the capsule switch. The capsule's dots only, never text. Must clear 3:1 on ground and panel. |
| `color.reading.machine` | `--mx-color-reading-machine` | `#ff5d4f` | `#b3261e` | `#ff5d4f` | `#b3261e` | Dot on the 機械用 side of the capsule switch. The capsule's dots only, never text. Must clear 3:1 on ground and panel. |
| `color.rule` | `--mx-color-rule` | `#1d4d2f` | `#7f9a86` | `#3d362c` | `#8fa093` | Hairline for decorative separators only. Never the only boundary of a control: it measures 1.5–2.4:1 and is exempt from contrast as decoration. |
| `color.scanline` | `--mx-color-scanline` | `#02080547` | `#ccd7c947` | `#100e0b47` | `#cdd6cb47` | Scan-line wash: ground at 28% alpha. Decoration only; contrast is measured without it. |
| `color.text` | `--mx-color-text` | `#c4f2d0` | `#0c2115` | `#ece4d4` | `#111b15` | Body text. Use for all running text. Must clear 7:1 on ground and panel. |
| `color.text-lead` | `--mx-color-text-lead` | `#eafff0` | `#03130a` | `#f0e0b4` | `#06281a` | Emphasised text for short runs: titles, strong, hover. Not for paragraphs at night. Must clear 7:1 on ground and panel. |
| `color.text-muted` | `--mx-color-text-muted` | `#80c194` | `#2a4735` | `#c2b496` | `#2f4236` | Secondary text: meta lines, captions, hints. Dim with this colour, never with opacity. Must clear 4.5:1 on ground and panel. |

## Scales

| Token | Custom property | Value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `border.width.hair` | `--mx-border-width-hair` | `1px` | Hairline border (1px). |
| `border.width.strong` | `--mx-border-width-strong` | `2px` | Strong border, and the focus ring width (2px). |
| `breakpoint.desk` | `--mx-breakpoint-desk` | `1100px` | Breakpoint desk (1100px). Media queries cannot read custom properties, so CSS uses this literal; lint allows only the four breakpoints. |
| `breakpoint.phone` | `--mx-breakpoint-phone` | `600px` | Breakpoint phone (600px). Media queries cannot read custom properties, so CSS uses this literal; lint allows only the four breakpoints. |
| `breakpoint.tablet` | `--mx-breakpoint-tablet` | `720px` | Breakpoint tablet (720px). Media queries cannot read custom properties, so CSS uses this literal; lint allows only the four breakpoints. |
| `breakpoint.wall` | `--mx-breakpoint-wall` | `1360px` | Breakpoint wall (1360px). Media queries cannot read custom properties, so CSS uses this literal; lint allows only the four breakpoints. |
| `font.family.dot` | `--mx-font-family-dot` | `"DotGothic16", "M PLUS 1 Code", ui-monospace, monospace` | Rain, boot, curtain and the rain switch. Never reading text. |
| `font.family.ja` | `--mx-font-family-ja` | `"M PLUS 1 Code", "IBM Plex Mono", ui-monospace, "Menlo", monospace` | Any run marked lang="ja": M PLUS 1 Code, then the mono stack. |
| `font.family.mono` | `--mx-font-family-mono` | `"IBM Plex Mono", "M PLUS 1 Code", ui-monospace, "Menlo", monospace` | Latin text, controls and code. |
| `font.leading.code` | `--mx-font-leading-code` | `1.75` | Line height for code blocks. |
| `font.leading.read` | `--mx-font-leading-read` | `2` | Line height for Japanese article body. |
| `font.leading.terminal` | `--mx-font-leading-terminal` | `1.6` | Line height for terminal output. |
| `font.leading.tight` | `--mx-font-leading-tight` | `1.25` | Tight line height for display lines. |
| `font.leading.title` | `--mx-font-leading-title` | `1.45` | Line height for titles. |
| `font.leading.ui` | `--mx-font-leading-ui` | `1.7` | Line height for page text and chrome. |
| `font.size.body` | `--mx-font-size-body` | `0.9375rem` | Page text (15px). |
| `font.size.entry.max` | `--mx-font-size-entry-max` | `2.125rem` | Entry names in stream rows, largest end (34px). |
| `font.size.entry.min` | `--mx-font-size-entry-min` | `1.375rem` | Entry names in stream rows, smallest end (22px). |
| `font.size.heading` | `--mx-font-size-heading` | `1.375rem` | Article h2 (22px). |
| `font.size.label` | `--mx-font-size-label` | `0.75rem` | Code language tab and Copy (12px). |
| `font.size.lead` | `--mx-font-size-lead` | `1.125rem` | Role line and article h3 (18px). |
| `font.size.meta` | `--mx-font-size-meta` | `0.8125rem` | Meta lines, hints, chips, the status line and the footer (13px). |
| `font.size.prompt.max` | `--mx-font-size-prompt-max` | `2.75rem` | The name as a terminal line, largest end (44px). |
| `font.size.prompt.min` | `--mx-font-size-prompt-min` | `1.75rem` | The name as a terminal line, smallest end (28px). |
| `font.size.rain` | `--mx-font-size-rain` | `16px` | Rain glyphs. DotGothic16 is drawn for 16px, so this is pixels on purpose. |
| `font.size.read` | `--mx-font-size-read` | `1.0625rem` | Article body from 720px (17px). |
| `font.size.read-compact` | `--mx-font-size-read-compact` | `1rem` | Article body below 720px, and the command field on touch (16px). |
| `font.size.title.max` | `--mx-font-size-title-max` | `2.375rem` | Article title, largest end of its fluid size (38px). |
| `font.size.title.min` | `--mx-font-size-title-min` | `1.5rem` | Article title, smallest end of its fluid size (24px). |
| `font.size.ui` | `--mx-font-size-ui` | `0.875rem` | Header, controls, terminal text and code blocks (14px). |
| `font.weight.bold` | `--mx-font-weight-bold` | `700` | Bold. The giant name only. |
| `font.weight.medium` | `--mx-font-weight-medium` | `500` | Medium weight for marks, labels and headings. |
| `font.weight.regular` | `--mx-font-weight-regular` | `400` | Regular weight for running text. |
| `layer.boot` | `--mx-layer-boot` | `30` | z-index of the boot layer. Every z-index comes from this list. |
| `layer.curtain` | `--mx-layer-curtain` | `40` | z-index of the curtain layer. Every z-index comes from this list. |
| `layer.lifted` | `--mx-layer-lifted` | `21` | z-index of the lifted layer. Every z-index comes from this list. |
| `layer.overlay` | `--mx-layer-overlay` | `22` | z-index of the overlay layer. Every z-index comes from this list. |
| `layer.rain` | `--mx-layer-rain` | `-1` | z-index of the rain layer. Every z-index comes from this list. |
| `layer.scanline` | `--mx-layer-scanline` | `20` | z-index of the scanline layer. Every z-index comes from this list. |
| `layer.skip` | `--mx-layer-skip` | `50` | z-index of the skip layer. Every z-index comes from this list. |
| `layer.status` | `--mx-layer-status` | `25` | z-index of the status layer. Every z-index comes from this list. |
| `motion.blink.count` | `--mx-motion-blink-count` | `5` | Cursor blinks five times, then stays lit. |
| `motion.blink.duration` | `--mx-motion-blink-duration` | `1000ms` | Cursor blink period. |
| `motion.boot.failsafe` | `--mx-motion-boot-failsafe` | `8000ms` | The intro ends no later than this. |
| `motion.decode.duration` | `--mx-motion-decode-duration` | `450ms` | Text settling out of corpus glyphs. |
| `motion.double.duration` | `--mx-motion-double-duration` | `200ms` | The name doubling on return to 人間用. |
| `motion.drip.duration` | `--mx-motion-drip-duration` | `3200ms` | One cycle of the drop through the idle strand of the switch. |
| `motion.echo.duration` | `--mx-motion-echo-duration` | `480ms` | Déjà vu. |
| `motion.rain.duration.max` | `--mx-motion-rain-duration-max` | `21s` | Longest fall of one rain column (21s). |
| `motion.rain.duration.min` | `--mx-motion-rain-duration-min` | `9s` | Shortest fall of one rain column (9s). |
| `motion.shell.fallback` | `--mx-motion-shell-fallback` | `4000ms` | After this the recorded session gets its scrolling page back. |
| `motion.strand.duration.max` | `--mx-motion-strand-duration-max` | `11s` | Longest fall of one stream strand (11s). |
| `motion.strand.duration.min` | `--mx-motion-strand-duration-min` | `5s` | Shortest fall of one stream strand (5s). |
| `motion.wipe.duration` | `--mx-motion-wipe-duration` | `240ms` | A side of the switch becoming current. |
| `motion.wipe.steps` | `--mx-motion-wipe-steps` | `3` | Steps of the wipe; compose as steps(var(--mx-motion-wipe-steps)). |
| `radius.capsule` | `--mx-radius-capsule` | `999px` | Fully rounded capsule ends. |
| `radius.control` | `--mx-radius-control` | `2px` | Corner radius of controls. Panels and the logo have no radius. |

| `size.logo.header-compact` | `--mx-size-logo-header-compact` | `32px` | Logo in the compact header (32px). |
| `size.measure.lede` | `--mx-size-measure-lede` | `68` | Measure of Latin ledes and captions, in ch (68ch). A number because DTCG dimensions allow only px, em and rem; use as calc(var(--mx-size-measure-lede) * 1ch). |

| `size.measure.read-compact` | `--mx-size-measure-read-compact` | `640px` | Article measure below 720px: 40 full-width characters at the body size. |

# Changelog

matrix's releases, written by hand (01, "Distribution and versioning"). TOMBO's releases,
`v0.1.0` to `v0.14.1`, are recorded on the `tombo` branch.

## 1.0.0-alpha.0

Unreleased. The foundation: an empty but real package.

- Tokens for the four contexts in DTCG 2025.10, compiled by Terrazzo to `tokens.css`,
  `tokens.json` and `tokens.d.ts`.
- Reset, base typography, the focus ring, `.mx-frame`, `.mx-vh`, `.mx-skip`.
- Self-hosted fonts: IBM Plex Mono, M PLUS 1 Code and DotGothic16 from Fontsource.
- Storybook 10 on the Astro framework: toolbar globals for palette, theme, motion, language
  and reading; Welcome and Foundations pages; accessibility at `error`; `npm run test:stories`.
- Visual regression in the pinned Playwright image (`npm run test:visual`), with committed baselines.
- `Head` and its pre-paint script, `Layout`, and `<mx-root>` for theme, palette, motion and
  flag-carrying links.
- Chrome: Header, Mark, Logo, Nav, Menu (`<mx-menu>`), Control (Hold rain, Operator colours,
  Daylight), Footer, Language link (draft).
- Surfaces: Panel, Lede, Figures, Inline list, Log, Meta, Status, Moved.
- Chrome strings in English and Japanese (`@wadakatu/matrix/strings`).
- Signature: Rain and Hold, Name, Stream and Streams, the reading Switch (`<mx-switch>`; rain,
  compact and capsule), Readings (`<mx-readings>`) with the in-place change on the Web Animations
  API and the `\` / `¥` shortcut with its off switch, Boot (`<mx-boot>`) and Curtain, decode and
  the three rewards, scan lines.
- `@wadakatu/matrix/lib`: the seeded build-time helpers (rain, strands, curtain, glyph pools,
  the name mask, decode frames, the film-name filter).
- Terminal (`<mx-terminal>`): one shell in one viewport that follows `visualViewport`, the
  recorded session without scripts and the fallback to it, the line editor, keys and block
  cursor, effects for the site's interpreter; Prompt, Guide, Chips, Status line, Takeover,
  Fetch card, Login card, Swatches, Run. The interpreter contract, the one renderer and a demo
  interpreter in `@wadakatu/matrix/lib`.
- Reading: Masthead and the article frame, Contents (`<mx-toc>`), Prose, Reference link, Code
  block with Copy (`<mx-copy>`), Share (`<mx-share>`), Post foot and Index; Shiki's
  `css-variables` theme mapped to the roles. Drafts, awaiting approval: code title, diff, callout,
  details, table, task list, footnotes. A print layer for articles: no rain, no chrome, the day
  ink on white, link addresses after absolute links.
- `npm run check`: token validity, contrast, golden values, no raw values, unknown tokens,
  freshness, the Baseline ledger, package contents and version consistency.

<!-- Source: src/effects/boot/boot.md -->

---
name: Boot
status: approved
class: mx-boot
element: mx-boot
attributes: [data-boot]
tokens: [color.ground, color.text-muted, color.accent, color.text-lead, font.family.dot, font.size.ui, font.leading.terminal, layer.boot, layer.lifted, space.3, space.4, space.10]
---

# Boot

## Purpose

The intro on the first visit to Home in a tab: the data file's keys, their real values decoding out
of corpus glyphs, then the logo, then the curtain (L1, L4, L5).

## Contract

```html
<mx-boot class="mx-boot">
  <div class="mx-boot-lines" aria-hidden="true">
    <p class="mx-boot-line"><span class="mx-boot-key">name</span><span class="mx-boot-value" data-text="wadakatu_">wadakatu_</span></p>
    <p class="mx-boot-line mx-boot-logo"><span class="mx-boot-key">logo</span><span class="mx-boot-mark"><img class="mx-logo" src="…" alt=""><span class="mx-boot-cover"></span></span></p>
  </div>
  <p class="mx-boot-exit">
    <button class="mx-control mx-boot-skip" type="button">Skip intro <kbd>Esc</kbd></button>
    <mx-switch class="mx-switch" role="group" aria-label="Reading">…</mx-switch>
    <span class="mx-boot-note">This site opens as a terminal. <span lang="ja">人間用</span> is the same site as an ordinary page.</span>
  </p>
</mx-boot>
```

First in `<mx-root>` (the Layout's `boot` slot), so Skip is the first tab stop while it is up. The
page passes `boot` to `Head` (or `Layout`), which puts the decision in the head script.

## Variants and states

- `data-boot="play"` on the root: shown; the rest of the page is hidden behind it.
- `data-boot="frozen"` (`?boot=frozen`): the still. Every line settled, the logo whole; no motion, no
  timeout, no script needed.
- No attribute: not shown. Never without scripts, never with reduced motion or `?motion=0`, never
  with `?run=`, and once per tab (`sessionStorage['mx-boot']`); `?boot=1` replays it.

## Behaviour

The head script decides it and ends it on Skip, Escape, a click or tap anywhere on it (either side of
its switch included) and `motion.boot.failsafe`, so it ends with every other script blocked. Ending
it removes `data-boot`, emits `mx:bootend` and moves focus to `main`. `mx-boot` adds the motion:
values decode (`decode`), the logo is wiped in from the top in ten steps by lifting a cover off it
(the image itself is never clipped, L5), the curtain falls, the boot
ends behind it, the curtain lifts. An early end drops the rest; reduced motion switched on ends it.
機械用 on its switch goes straight to the shell; 人間用 is Skip.

## Tokens

`color.ground`, `color.text-muted`, `color.accent`, `color.text-lead`; `font.family.dot`,
`font.size.ui`, `font.leading.terminal`; `layer.boot`, `layer.lifted` (the cover over the logo);
`space.3`, `space.4`, `space.10`. The line size `--mx-text-boot` is the effect's own fluid formula.
`motion.boot.failsafe` is read by the head script, which ends the boot (Head).

## Accessibility

The lines are `aria-hidden` (they repeat facts on the page). Skip is focused when it starts, so
Enter, Space and Escape all end it; the note says what comes next and that 人間用 exists. Flashing:
one direction per transition; checked frame by frame (05).

## Do / Don't

- Do keep it to Home, once per tab.
- Don't let anything but the head script decide it.
- Don't scramble the logo: it is wiped in whole.
- Don't clip, mask or transform the image to wipe it: the cover moves, the mark does not (L5).

name: Callout
status: draft
class: mx-callout
attributes: [data-variant]
tokens: [color.accent, color.ground, color.rule, color.text-muted, font.size.meta, font.weight.medium, font.leading.ui, border.width.hair, border.width.strong, space.1, space.3, space.4]
---

# Callout

## Purpose

`:::message` and `:::message alert`: a note inside the article, told apart by its word, not by a hue
(L7). A draft (04): not approved until wadakatu has seen it.

## Contract

```html
<aside class="mx-callout">
  <p class="mx-callout-label">Note</p>
  <p>…</p>
</aside>
```

The alert adds `data-variant="alert"`; its label is the Warning string.

## Variants and states

| | Message (default) | Alert (`data-variant="alert"`) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Box | `ground`, hairline `rule`, padding 12px by 16px | The same |
| Left rule | 2px `text-muted` | 2px `accent` |
| Label | Note / メモ, `text-muted` | `!` (generated), then Warning / 警告, `accent` |

The label is `meta` size, medium, in the page's chrome face; the body is Prose as outside the box,
4px under the label, 12px between blocks.

## Behaviour

No element. Static; complete without scripts.

## Tokens

`color.accent`, `color.ground`, `color.rule`, `color.text-muted`; `font.size.meta`,
`font.weight.medium`, `font.leading.ui`; `border.width.hair`, `border.width.strong`; `space.1`,
`space.3`, `space.4`.

## Accessibility

An `aside`, as Zenn writes it; never `role="alert"`, which is a live region. The label is real text,
so the two variants differ by their word in forced colours and on paper; the `!` has empty
alternative text. Nothing in it takes focus but the author's links. Printed with `break-inside: avoid`.

## Do / Don't

- Do let it hold whatever Prose holds.
- Don't give the alert a hue of its own.
- Don't use it for a message that has just appeared.

# Chips

## Purpose

Suggested commands to tap, and on touch the keys a phone keyboard lacks (L3).

## Contract

```html
<div class="mx-chips" role="group" aria-label="Keys and suggested commands">
  <button class="mx-chip" type="button" data-key="Tab" aria-label="Complete">tab</button>
  <button class="mx-chip" type="button" data-key="ArrowUp" aria-label="Previous command">↑</button>
  <button class="mx-chip" type="button" data-key="ArrowDown" aria-label="Next command">↓</button>
  <button class="mx-chip" type="button" data-key="C-c" aria-label="Cancel">^C</button>
  <button class="mx-chip" type="button" data-run="help">help</button>
</div>
```

## Variants and states

- One row that scrolls sideways in itself. Hover: `text-lead` on an `accent` border.
- Coarse pointer: bigger chips, and the four key chips first (`accent` on `control-border`).
  Fine pointer: the key chips are absent.
- Absent without scripts.

## Behaviour

`mx-terminal` runs a chip's command, or presses its key (Tab, Up, Down, Ctrl+C), without moving focus:
a phone's keyboard stays as it was, and a desktop field keeps focus.

## Tokens

`color.text-muted`, `color.text-lead`, `color.accent`, `color.ground`, `color.rule`,
`color.control-border`; `font.size.meta`; `radius.control`; `border.width.hair`; `space.0-5`,
`space.1-5`, `space.2`, `space.3`.

## Accessibility

Buttons in a labelled group; the key chips have names (`Complete`, `Previous command`, `Next command`,
`Cancel`). A chip's border is `rule`, decoration: its label identifies it (05, rule 4). Every chip is
at least 24px tall. Keyboard: each chip is a tab stop after the screen.

## Do / Don't

- Do put the keys first on touch.
- Don't move focus when a chip runs.
- Don't add a chip for a command the interpreter does not have.

name: Code block
status: approved
class: mx-code
element: mx-copy
attributes: [data-diff]
tokens: [color.accent, color.ground, color.on-accent, color.rule, color.text, color.text-lead, color.text-muted, font.family.mono, font.size.ui, font.size.label, font.leading.code, font.weight.medium, font.weight.regular, border.width.hair, space.0-5, space.3, space.4, space.10]
---

# Code block

## Purpose

Code in an article: the ground cut into the panel, its language as a tab, and Copy. Shiki's
`css-variables` theme reads the roles, so code follows all four contexts (L7). The block and Copy are
approved; the title and the diff are drafts (04).

## Contract

```html
<div class="mx-code">
  <pre class="astro-code css-variables" data-language="bash" tabindex="0"><code><span class="line">…</span></code></pre>
  <mx-copy class="mx-copy" data-copied="Copied" data-failed="Not copied"><button type="button">Copy</button></mx-copy>
</div>
```

The `<pre>` is the highlighter's, as written (Astro's Shiki step, `wrap: true`); `CodeBlock.astro`
takes it as its slot and adds the wrapper and Copy. The site's Markdown step writes the same markup.

Drafts:

```html
<figure class="mx-code">
  <figcaption class="mx-code-title">config/fixture.php</figcaption>
  <pre data-language="php"><code>…</code></pre>
  <mx-copy class="mx-copy" data-copied="Copied" data-failed="Not copied"><button type="button">Copy</button></mx-copy>
</figure>

<div class="mx-code" data-diff>
  <pre data-language="js"><code><span class="line"> const a = 1;</span>
<span class="line" data-diff="del">-const b = 2;</span>
<span class="line" data-diff="add">+const b = 3;</span></code></pre>
  …
</div>
```

## Variants and states

- Default: `ui` size, `leading.code`, 40px of top padding under the tab; the tab is the language
  (`plaintext` when the fence names none), drawn from `data-language`, `text-muted`.
- Copy: `text-muted` on `ground`, `text-lead` on hover; for 1.6s after a press it says Copied on an
  `accent` fill (Highlight in forced colours), or Not copied.
- Title (draft): the file name in the tab's place, in the flow, `text-lead`; it wraps anywhere and
  keeps clear of Copy; the code starts 16px below it.
- Diff (draft): every line hangs by two characters. Added: `+`, medium, `text-lead`. Removed: `-`,
  regular, `text-muted`. Unchanged: a space, `text`, with its syntax colours. Inside a changed line
  every token takes the line's tone. No fill, no strike-through, no hue.

## Behaviour

`mx-copy` copies the text of the block's `<code>` (a diff comes back with its signs, so it applies).
Without scripts it is not shown; the code is complete and selectable (05).

## Tokens

`color.accent`, `color.ground`, `color.on-accent`, `color.rule`, `color.text`, `color.text-lead`,
`color.text-muted`; `font.family.mono`, `font.size.ui`, `font.size.label`, `font.leading.code`,
`font.weight.medium`, `font.weight.regular`; `border.width.hair`; `space.0-5`, `space.3`, `space.4`,
`space.10`. Shiki's variables map to roles: foreground and parameter `text`; comment and punctuation
`text-muted`; keyword, function and link `accent`; constant and strings `text-lead`; inserted
`text-lead`, deleted `text-muted`, changed `text`.

## Accessibility

The `<pre>` is focusable (Shiki's `tabindex="0"`) and shows the ring. The tab is generated with empty
alternative text; a title is real text, the figure's caption. Copy is a button after the code, in the
page and focus order, 25px tall and at least 44px wide, its ring inside the box. A diff's state is its
sign and its weight, so it reads without colour, in forced colours and on paper. In print: no Copy,
the rule, tab or title and syntax colours kept (05).

## Do / Don't

- Do keep the highlighter's `<pre>` as written.
- Don't render Copy as a dead button without scripts.
- Don't mark added and removed lines by colour alone.

# Contents

## Purpose

The article's sections, so a long Japanese post can be read in any order: every `h2` numbered from
01, its `h3` under it.

## Contract

```html
<mx-toc>
  <aside class="mx-toc mx-panel">
    <details>
      <summary class="mx-toc-summary">Contents</summary>
      <nav aria-label="Contents">
        <ol>
          <li><a href="#intro">…</a></li>
          <li><a href="#setup">…</a><ol><li><a href="#before" aria-current="location">…</a></li></ol></li>
        </ol>
      </nav>
    </details>
  </aside>
</mx-toc>
```

`Toc.astro` takes the headings as Astro's Markdown rendering returns them (`depth`, `slug`, `text`);
`h4` are not listed.

## Variants and states

- Below 1100px: a disclosure above the body, closed; `▸` / `▾` before the word.
- From 1100px: a rail, `size.rail` wide, sticky 20px from the top and scrolling inside itself when
  taller than the window. Always open: the summary gives way to a label drawn from the nav's own name.
  An engine without `::details-content` keeps the disclosure, and the element opens it.
- The section being read: `text-lead` and a 2px `accent` rule at its left (`aria-current="location"`).
- Links are `text-muted`, numbers `accent`, rules between sections dotted `rule`.

## Behaviour

`mx-toc` marks the section being read: the last heading whose top has passed 96px down the window.
Below 1100px choosing a section closes the disclosure. Without scripts the disclosure and every link
work; the mark is absent (05).

## Tokens

`color.accent`, `color.rule`, `color.text-lead`, `color.text-muted`; `font.family.mono`,
`font.size.meta`, `font.weight.medium`; `border.width.hair`, `border.width.strong`; `size.target`,
`size.measure.*` (`--mx-measure`); `space.2`, `space.3`, `space.4`, `space.5`.

## Accessibility

An `aside` holding a `nav` named Contents (目次). The summary is a native disclosure, 44px tall, its
marker generated with empty alternative text; focus ring inside the box. Keyboard: Tab to the
summary, Enter or Space opens it, Tab through the links; from 1100px straight to the links. The mark
is the word's colour and a rule, never colour alone. A heading in the other language carries `lang`.
Not printed (05).

## Do / Don't

- Do build it from the rendered headings, so the fragments match.
- Don't list `h4`.
- Don't animate the disclosure.

<!-- Source: src/components/control/control.md -->

---
name: Control
status: approved
class: mx-control
attributes: [aria-pressed, data-action]
tokens: [color.text, color.text-lead, color.ground, color.control-border, color.accent, color.on-accent, color.focus, font.size.ui, font.leading.ui, radius.control, border.width.hair, border.width.strong, space.1, space.2, space.3]
---

# Control

## Purpose

One look for a button, a link, and a label wrapping a checkbox. It is also the chrome's three
controls: Hold rain, Operator colours and Daylight (L4, L7).

## Contract

```html
<label class="mx-control" data-action="hold"><input type="checkbox"> Hold rain</label>
<button class="mx-control" data-action="palette" type="button" aria-pressed="false">Operator colours</button>
<button class="mx-control" data-action="theme" type="button" aria-pressed="false">Daylight</button>
```

On a page with two readings the shortcut's off switch is one more:
`<label class="mx-control" data-action="shortcut"><input type="checkbox" checked> Enable <kbd>\</kbd> / <kbd>¥</kbd> shortcut</label>`
(Readings).

A plain control is `<button class="mx-control" type="button">` or `<a class="mx-control" href>`.

## Variants and states

- Rest: `text` on `ground`, a 1px `control-border` box. Hover: `text-lead`, `accent` border.
- Pressed (`aria-pressed="true"`): filled `accent` with `on-accent` text.
- `data-action="hold"`: a checkbox in the label, `accent` tick. Hidden when motion is off,
  because then nothing moves. Present in both readings.
- `data-action="shortcut"`: a checked checkbox; hidden until `mx-readings` is defined, so a page
  without two readings, or without scripts, never shows it.
- `data-action="palette"`, `data-action="theme"`: hidden until `mx-root` is defined; the
  theme toggle is also hidden where `light-dark()` is missing (03).

## Behaviour

No element of its own. `mx-root` drives the toggles: Daylight sets `data-theme` and stores
`mx-theme`; Operator colours sets `data-palette` and rewrites the address and every in-site link,
storing nothing (decision Q4); Hold rain sets `data-rain="held"`. Without scripts Hold rain still
works through `:has()`, and the two toggles are absent.

## Tokens

`color.text`, `color.text-lead`, `color.ground`, `color.control-border`, `color.accent`,
`color.on-accent`, `color.focus`; `font.size.ui`, `font.leading.ui`; `radius.control`;
`border.width.hair`, `border.width.strong`; `space.1`, `space.2`, `space.3`.

## Accessibility

Buttons expose `aria-pressed`. The Hold rain label is outlined when its checkbox has focus
(the replacement for the checkbox's own ring, 05). Keyboard: Tab to each; Space toggles; Enter
presses a button. Every control is at least 24px tall, 44px in the phone menu.
In forced colours a pressed button is `Highlight` with `HighlightText`; the checkbox shows its
own state.

## Do / Don't

- Do use `control-border` for a control's box; `rule` is decoration.
- Don't render a toggle that needs scripts as a dead button.
- Don't set the pressed state with a class.

name: Curtain

# Curtain

## Purpose

Slabs of the site's running text that cover the page as the boot ends (L1).

## Contract

```html
<div class="mx-curtain" aria-hidden="true">
  <span class="mx-curtain-slab" lang="ja">…</span>
</div>
```

24 slabs of 260 glyphs from `curtainSlabs(phrases)`. Last in `<mx-root>` (the Layout's `curtain` slot).

## Variants and states

- Hidden; `data-on` while `mx-boot` runs its last step. Never shown in a still, without scripts, or
  with reduced motion.

## Behaviour

`mx-boot` drops the slabs in a fixed scatter, ends the boot behind them, and lifts them. Under 1s.

## Tokens

`color.ground`, `color.rain.body`, `color.rain.head`; `font.family.dot`, `font.size.rain`,
`font.leading.tight`; `layer.curtain`.

## Accessibility

`aria-hidden`, no pointer events. One fall and one lift, never an alternation (05, "Flashing").

## Do / Don't

- Do feed it the same corpus as the rain.
- Don't use it as a general transition.

<!-- Source: src/effects/decode/decode.md -->

---
name: Decode
status: approved
attributes: []
tokens: []
---

# Decode

## Purpose

Text that settles out of the corpus's own glyphs into its real words, for the effects that change
text in place (L1, L4).

## Contract

```ts
import { decode, textTween, pools, moving, held } from "./decode.ts";
decode(el, 450, { delay: 80, allWide: true }); // returns a TextTween: { anim, end() }
```

```html
<mx-root data-wide="…" data-narrow="…">…<span data-text="wadakatu_">wadakatu_</span>…</mx-root>
```

The final text is the element's `data-text`, or its text when it is called. The pools are
`data-wide` and `data-narrow` on `<mx-root>`, which Layout writes from the site's corpus.

## Variants and states

- `allWide`: every frame draws from the wide pool (the boot's values, the switch side just taken).
- `delay`: the tween waits before it starts (the headings of a change of reading, staggered).

## Behaviour

A module, not an element: Boot, Readings and Rewards call it. Each tween is a target-less Web
Animations `Animation` whose progress one shared frame loop reads, so delay, `finish()` and
`cancel()` are the platform's. `end()` cancels it and writes the final text at once. `moving()` is
false with `data-motion="off"` or reduced motion; `held()` is true while rain is held. Every caller
checks `moving()`, and Readings and Rewards `held()`, before they decode. Without scripts the text is
the final text from the start.

## Tokens

None. The callers pass the duration: 450ms in Readings, the value of `motion.decode.duration`; Boot's
and Rewards' are their own numbers.

## Accessibility

The final text is in the markup. A tween replaces the element's text frame by frame and leaves the
final text when it ends or is ended. A change of reading is announced by Status, not by the text
that decodes; the boot's lines and the rewards' layers are `aria-hidden`.

## Do / Don't

- Do give it the site's corpus; never a placeholder glyph set (L1).
- Don't start one when `moving()` is false.

# Details

## Purpose

`:::details title`: part of the article folded away, a native disclosure boxed as the login card is.
A draft (04): not approved until wadakatu has seen it.

## Contract

```html
<details class="mx-details">
  <summary class="mx-details-summary">A fixture example</summary>
  <div class="mx-details-body">…</div>
</details>
```

## Variants and states

- Closed: a hairline `rule` box, no fill; the summary at least 44px tall, 16px inline padding, `accent`,
  medium, Prose's size at `leading.title`, `▸` before it.
- Open: `▾`, a hairline under the summary, the body with 16px padding and 12px between blocks.
- Starts closed, as Zenn writes it. In print it is open, with `▾`.

## Behaviour

Native, with no element. It does not animate (no row in the motion catalogue, 05).

## Tokens

`color.accent`, `color.rule`; `font.weight.medium`, `font.leading.title`; `border.width.hair`;

# Fetch card

## Purpose

neofetch's card: the real mark beside key and value lines (L1, L5).

## Contract

```html
<div class="mx-fetch">
  <img class="mx-logo mx-fetch-mark" src="/assets/logo/logo-400.png" alt="fixture_ logo" width="400" height="400" />
  <div class="mx-fetch-side"><div class="mx-ln">…</div></div>
</div>
```

## Variants and states

- From 600px the mark stands beside the lines, `clamp(132px, 26vmin, 224px)`; below, above them at 112px.
- Values that wrap stay in their own column. The mark takes the palette filter (operator-night).

## Behaviour

Printed by `render` from a card item (`{ card: { src, alt, width, height }, lines }`), at build time
and live. No behaviour of its own.

## Tokens

`space.1-5`, `space.2`. The lines read the line tones (Terminal); the mark reads the Logo's.

## Accessibility

The image has the interpreter's `alt`. The swatches row is decoration (`aria-hidden`).

## Do / Don't

- Do use the designer's file, whole and square.
- Don't draw the mark out of characters.
- Don't put a fact only in the image.

name: Foundations
status: approved
attributes: [data-reading]
tokens: [color.ground, color.text, color.text-lead, color.accent, color.on-accent, color.focus, font.family.mono, font.family.ja, font.size.body, font.size.entry.min, font.size.entry.max, font.size.prompt.min, font.size.prompt.max, font.size.title.min, font.size.title.max, font.weight.regular, font.leading.ui, border.width.hair, border.width.strong, radius.control, size.frame, size.measure.read, size.measure.read-compact, layer.skip, space.1, space.1-5, space.2, space.3, space.4]
---

# Foundations

## Purpose

What every page has before any component: the layer order, the reset, base type, links, the focus
ring, the derived properties, and the three utilities `.mx-frame`, `.mx-vh` and `.mx-skip` (L2, L6).

## Contract

```css
@layer mx.reset, mx.tokens, mx.base, mx.components, mx.effects, mx.utilities;
```

```html
<a class="mx-skip" href="#main">Skip to content</a>
<main id="main" class="mx-frame" tabindex="-1">…</main>
<span class="mx-vh">Read by assistive technology only</span>
```

`@wadakatu/matrix/css` is `index.css` (the layer statement), the tokens, `reset.css`, `base.css`,
every component and effect, then `utilities.css`.

## Variants and states

- Reset (`mx.reset`): `border-box`, no body margin, no margins on headings, paragraphs and lists, no
  list markers.
- Base (`mx.base`): `ground` on the page; body text `text` in `font.family.mono`, `body` size,
  `leading.ui`; `:lang(ja)` in `font.family.ja` with strict line breaking, and Japanese headings
  broken by phrase. Links inherit their colour with a `hair` underline at a `space.1` offset; hover is
  `text-lead` with a `strong` underline. `kbd` is boxed; `::selection` is `accent` with `on-accent`.
- Derived properties (02): `--mx-pad`, `--mx-text-display`, `--mx-text-entry`, `--mx-text-prompt`,
  `--mx-text-title`, `--mx-measure` (`size.measure.read-compact`, `read` from 720px) and `--mx-inset`.
- Focus ring: `:focus-visible` is a `border.width.strong` outline in `color.focus`, 3px out. `main`
  shows none when the skip link moves focus there.
- `.mx-frame`: at most `size.frame` wide, centred, `--mx-pad` at the sides; unbounded in 機械用
  (`:root[data-reading="machine"]`).
- `.mx-skip`: above the top edge until focused, then `space.3` from the top, `accent` with
  `on-accent`, on `layer.skip`.
- Print: day colours, no painted ground or panel, and no skip link or status region (05, "Print").

## Behaviour

CSS only.

## Tokens

`color.ground`, `color.text`, `color.text-lead`, `color.accent`, `color.on-accent`, `color.focus`;
`font.family.mono`, `font.family.ja`, `font.size.body`, `font.weight.regular`, `font.leading.ui`, and
the `.min` and `.max` of `font.size.entry`, `font.size.prompt` and `font.size.title` (the derived
sizes); `border.width.hair`, `border.width.strong`; `radius.control`; `size.frame`,
`size.measure.read`, `size.measure.read-compact`; `layer.skip`; `space.1`, `space.1-5`, `space.2`,
`space.3`, `space.4`.

## Accessibility

The skip link is the first tab stop and moves focus to `main`. The ring clears 3:1 on `ground` and
`panel` in every context. `.mx-vh` hides text from sight, not from assistive technology. Text is
dimmed with colour, never `opacity` (L2).

## Do / Don't

- Do load `index.css` first, so the layer order holds.
- Do read the derived properties rather than repeat their formulas.
- Don't remove the focus ring.

# Guide

## Purpose

The first row of 機械用: what this is, in plain words, and the way to 人間用 for a reader who did not
ask for a shell (L3).

## Contract

```html
<p class="mx-guide">
  <span class="mx-guide-say">This site opens as a terminal.<span class="mx-guide-live"> Type <kbd>help</kbd>, or tap a command below.</span></span>
  <a class="mx-control mx-guide-way" data-to="human" href="/human/">Read it as an ordinary page: <span lang="ja">人間用</span></a>
  <button class="mx-control mx-guide-hide" type="button" aria-label="Hide this note">×</button>
</p>
```

## Variants and states

- Live: the sentence, the hint to type, the link and the ×. Recorded (no scripts): the sentence and the
  link only.
- Below 720px the sentence is for assistive technology only; the row is one 44px link and a 44px ×.
- Hidden: after ×, for the rest of the tab; while an on-screen keyboard is up.
- The link has an `accent` border and fills on hover. All four contexts read roles only.

## Behaviour

The link is an `a[data-to="human"]`, so `mx-readings` makes it the in-place change; without scripts it
is a plain link to the static twin. The × (`mx-terminal`) hides the row, remembers that in
`sessionStorage['mx-guide']` and puts focus in the field. It belongs to the page, not the session:
`clear` leaves it and it does not scroll.

## Tokens

`color.text-muted`, `color.text`, `color.text-lead`, `color.accent`, `color.on-accent`, `color.rule`;
`font.size.meta`; `size.target`; `border.width.hair`; `space.0-5`, `space.1-5`, `space.2`, `space.3`.

## Accessibility

A paragraph with a link named by its text and a button named `Hide this note`. Keyboard: Tab to the
link, then the ×. Focus: the 2px ring. The × is identified by its glyph and name, not by its border
(`rule`, decoration).

## Do / Don't

- Do keep the way to 人間用 in the first row.
- Don't hide the row by itself when a command runs.
- Don't put the sentence anywhere it scrolls away.

<!-- Source: src/head/head.md -->

---
name: Head
status: approved
attributes: [data-theme, data-palette, data-motion, data-boot, data-shell]
tokens: [color.ground, motion.boot.failsafe, motion.shell.fallback]
---

# Head

## Purpose

The page's meta and the pre-paint script, which sets the root's attributes before the first paint so
that no frame shows the wrong theme, palette or motion (L4, L7).

## Contract

```html
<meta charset="utf-8" />
<meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1" />
<meta name="color-scheme" content="dark light" />
<meta name="theme-color" content="…" />
<title>…</title>
<meta name="description" content="…" />
<script>(() => { … })();</script>
```

`Head.astro` takes `title`, `description`, `flags` (the site's own code, run inside the script) and
`boot`. `@wadakatu/matrix/head` exports the script as a string (`headScript(site, { boot })`), the
flag lists (`FLAGS.carried`: `palette`, `motion`; `FLAGS.spent`: `theme`, `boot`, `run`, `mode`) and
the storage keys `THEME_KEY` (`mx-theme`) and `BOOT_KEY` (`mx-boot`). The stylesheets are the site
layout's own imports.

## Variants and states

What the script sets on `<html>`:

- `data-theme="day"`: `?theme=day`, or `localStorage['mx-theme']` is `day`.
- `data-palette="operator"`: `?palette=operator`. Never read from storage.
- `data-motion="off"`: `?motion=0`, or the system asks for reduced motion.
- `data-boot="play"` or `"frozen"`: with `boot` only (Boot's page).
- `data-shell="recorded"`: after `motion.shell.fallback`, when the page has an `<mx-terminal>` that
  has not gone live.

## Behaviour

Inline and synchronous: it runs before the body is parsed, with no other script loaded. It sets
`theme-color` to `color.ground` of the context. Reads of storage never throw. Until `mx-root` is
defined, a page whose palette or motion came from the address gets them on every in-site link at
`DOMContentLoaded`, so the flags travel with the controller blocked. With `boot` it decides the intro
and ends it on Escape, a click on it, or `motion.boot.failsafe`.

## Tokens

`color.ground` (each context's, for `theme-color`), `motion.boot.failsafe` and
`motion.shell.fallback`, read by id from `dist/tokens.json` when the script is built.

## Accessibility

No visible output. Reduced motion from the system is honoured before the first paint, and the boot
moves focus to `main` when it ends.

## Do / Don't

- Do put it first in `<head>`, inline, so that a Content Security Policy can allow it by hash.
- Don't store the palette: the address carries it (03).

# Header

## Purpose

The page's one row of chrome: the Mark, the Nav and the controls (L7: the palette and the
theme are chosen here).

## Contract

```html
<header class="mx-header mx-frame">
  <a class="mx-mark" href="/">…</a>
  <mx-menu><details class="mx-menu">
    <summary class="mx-control"><span class="mx-menu-label">Menu</span></summary>
    <nav class="mx-nav" aria-label="Main">…</nav>
    <div class="mx-controls">
      <mx-switch class="mx-switch" role="group" aria-label="Reading">…</mx-switch>
      <label class="mx-control" data-action="hold">…</label>
      <button class="mx-control" data-action="palette" …>…</button>
      <button class="mx-control" data-action="theme" …>…</button>
      <a class="mx-lang" href="/ja/" hreflang="ja" lang="ja">日本語</a>
    </div>
  </details></mx-menu>
</header>
```

The language link is rendered only where the page has a twin.

## Variants and states

- 69px tall at 1440 and 53px below 720px, in both readings.
- 機械用: the bottom rule is dashed, and the Nav is a window list.
- Below 720px: one row (the Mark, the menu button, the switch); the rest unfolds from the Menu.

## Behaviour

No element of its own; `mx-menu` and `mx-root` work inside it. Without scripts the menu is a
native disclosure and Hold rain works; Daylight and Operator colours are absent.

## Tokens

`color.ground`, `color.rule`, `font.size.ui`, `border.width.hair`, `space.2`, `space.3`, `space.7`.

## Accessibility

A `header` landmark. Tab order: Mark, nav links, the switch, Hold rain, Operator colours,
Daylight, the language link; below 720px, Mark, Menu, the switch, and the menu's contents when open.

## Do / Don't

- Do keep it out of the page's flow of reading: it is not sticky.
- Don't add items between the nav and the controls; the order is the Tab order.

# Inline list

## Purpose

A wrapping row of words or links: skills, a panel's trailing links, an entry's addresses.

## Contract

```html
<ul class="mx-inline-list"><li>TypeScript</li><li>Astro</li></ul>
<p class="mx-inline-list" data-variant="after"><a href="/projects/">All projects</a> <a href="/blog/">Read the blog</a></p>
<p class="mx-inline-list" data-variant="links"><a href="https://…">example.com</a></p>
```

## Variants and states

- Default: a list of words, 4px by 20px apart (the prototype's `.skills`).
- `data-variant="after"`: a panel's trailing links, 4px by 28px, 20px above (`.after`).
- `data-variant="links"`: an entry's addresses at `meta` size in `text-muted`, 4px by 24px (`.links`).

## Behaviour

No element.

## Tokens

`color.text-muted`, `font.size.meta`, `space.1`, `space.3`, `space.5`, `space.6`, `space.7`.

## Accessibility

Words are a list; links are a paragraph of links. A run in the other language carries `lang`.

## Do / Don't

- Do let it wrap; long addresses break anywhere.
- Don't use it for navigation: that is the Nav.

# Language link

## Purpose

A plain link to the same page in the other language, so a reader can change language without a
bilingual page (L6, decision Q8). Draft: designed from existing tokens, after TOMBO's header link.

## Contract

```html
<a class="mx-lang" href="/ja/" hreflang="ja" lang="ja">日本語</a>
```

On a Japanese page: `<a class="mx-lang" href="/" hreflang="en" lang="en">English</a>`.

## Variants and states

In the header's controls, after Daylight: `text-muted`, no underline, `text-lead` on hover.
Below 720px it is a 44px line of the open menu, under a dotted rule.

## Behaviour

No element; a plain link. Not rendered on articles, which have no twin (decision Q8).

## Tokens

`color.text-muted`, `color.text-lead`, `color.rule`, `size.target`, `space.2`, `border.width.hair`.

## Accessibility

Named in the language it leads to, with `lang` on the link and `hreflang` for the target.

## Do / Don't

- Do name the link in its own language (`日本語`, `English`).
- Don't render it where there is no twin.

# Layout

## Purpose

The page frame every page of the site shares: skip link, rain, header, `main`, footer and the status
region inside `<mx-root>`, with every root attribute at its no-script value in the markup (L4, L7).

## Contract

```html
<!doctype html>
<html lang="en" data-theme="night" data-reading="human">
  <head><!-- Head --><!-- slot "head" --></head>
  <body>
    <mx-root data-wide="…" data-narrow="…">
      <!-- slot "boot" -->
      <a class="mx-skip" href="#main">Skip to content</a>
      <!-- slot "rain" -->
      <header class="mx-header">…</header>
      <main id="main" class="mx-frame" tabindex="-1">…</main>
      <footer class="mx-footer">…</footer>
      <p class="mx-status mx-vh" role="status"></p>
      <!-- slot "curtain" -->
    </mx-root>
  </body>
</html>
```

Props: `title`, `description`, `lang`, `reading`, `mark`, `nav`, `footer`, `alternate` (the twin in
the other language), `flags` and `boot` (passed to Head), and `corpus`, whose glyph pools become
`data-wide` and `data-narrow` for Decode. Slots: the default (inside `main`), `head`, `boot`, `rain`,
`switch` (in the header), `footer` and `curtain`. The site imports the stylesheets and
`@wadakatu/matrix/elements` itself.

## Variants and states

- `reading` given: `data-reading` on `<html>`, and the shortcut's off switch in the header's menu and
  in the footer, with its hint.
- No `reading` (a document with one reading): none of those.
- Everything else on the root is the head script's and `mx-root`'s (Head, Root).

## Behaviour

No element of its own; `<mx-root>` is Root. Without scripts the page is the markup: night, phosphor,
the route's reading.

## Tokens

None directly; the parts read their own.

## Accessibility

The skip link is the first tab stop and moves focus to `main` (Foundations); one `main`, one status
region; `lang` on `<html>` is the page's language (L6), and the strings follow it.

## Do / Don't

- Do pass `alternate` only when the twin exists.
- Don't put anything before the skip link but the boot.

# Login card

The login command's fetch card as a disclosure on a phone, so the prompt has the screen (L3).

## Contract

```html
<details class="mx-login">
  <summary class="mx-login-summary" aria-label="who am I? fixture_, Fixture developer">who am I?</summary>
  <div class="mx-ln mx-ln-echo">…</div>
```

- From 720px: the summary is gone and the card is its contents, open or closed, the same as a session
  that printed in the open (`::details-content`; the live shell also sets `open` there for engines
  without it).

`mx-terminal` wraps the login command's output in it when `data-login` is set; a typed `neofetch`, or

# Logo

## Purpose

The mark by Chisato Satoh, shown whole wherever it appears (L5). The file is not MIT and is
not in the package: the site serves it and passes its address.

## Contract

```html
<img class="mx-logo" src="/images/logo-400.png" width="400" height="400" alt="">
```

`alt` is empty where a name sits beside it (the Mark); elsewhere it names the mark.

## Variants and states

Sizes are set by the component that holds it: 44px in the header, 32px in the compact header
(`size.logo.header`, `size.logo.header-compact`). In operator-night only, a filter tints it
(`--mx-logo-filter`: `hue-rotate(-80deg) saturate(1.15)`), which moves no pixel; in the other
three contexts it is the file as designed. The tint follows the nearest theme scope, so a day
or phosphor scope inside an operator-night page shows it untinted.

## Behaviour

No element.

## Tokens

None directly; its holders read `size.logo.*`. The filter is the derived property
`--mx-logo-filter` (02, "Derived properties").

## Accessibility

An image; decorative (`alt=""`) when the link beside it is named. In forced colours it is
shown as it is.

## Do / Don't

- Do use the designer's file and give it its intrinsic `width` and `height`.
- Don't crop, round, rotate, mask, transform or redraw it (L5), or set it in glyphs.
- Don't recolour it except by the operator-night filter.

# Mark

## Purpose

The home link at the start of the header: the logo, then the wordmark that names the link (L5).

## Contract

```html
<a class="mx-mark" href="/">
  <img class="mx-logo" src="/images/logo-400.png" width="400" height="400" alt="">wadakatu_
</a>
```

## Variants and states

One. Below 720px the logo is 32px and the link is at least 44px tall. The wordmark is `accent`
in every context; on hover it takes the base link's `text-lead`.

## Behaviour

No element; a plain link.

## Tokens

`color.accent`; `font.size.read-compact` (16px, the wordmark's size: no role names it, and this
is the scale step with the prototype's value); `font.weight.medium`; `size.logo.header`,
`size.logo.header-compact`; `size.target`. The 14px and 10px gaps and the 1.5 leading are the
prototype's one-off numbers.

## Accessibility

A link named by its wordmark; the logo inside it is `alt=""`. The focus ring is the base ring.

## Do / Don't

- Do give the wordmark as text, so it names the link.
- Don't give the logo `alt` text here: the name would be read twice.

<!-- Source: src/components/masthead/masthead.md -->

---
name: Masthead
status: approved
class: mx-masthead
attributes: [aria-current]
tokens: [color.accent, color.text-lead, color.text-muted, font.family.ja, font.family.mono, font.size.title.min, font.size.title.max, font.size.meta, font.weight.medium, font.leading.title, font.leading.ui, size.measure.read, size.measure.read-compact, size.rail, space.0-5, space.1, space.1-5, space.6, space.7]
---

# Masthead

## Purpose

The head of an article: where it is, what it is called, when it was written and what it is about,
with a strip of its own words beside it (L1).

## Contract

```html
<article class="mx-post">
  <header class="mx-masthead mx-panel">
    <div class="mx-stream-fall" aria-hidden="true">
      <span class="mx-strand" style="--j:0"><span class="mx-drop" style="--t:7.1s;--d:-3.2s;--rest:20%">…</span></span>
    </div>
    <div class="mx-masthead-id">
      <nav class="mx-crumb" aria-label="Breadcrumb"><a href="/human/" aria-label="Home">~</a>/<a href="/blog/">posts</a>/<span aria-current="page">3fa91c07d2b8e6.md</span></nav>
      <h1 class="mx-masthead-title">…</h1>
      <p class="mx-meta"><time datetime="2025-07-31">2025-07-31</time> <span>Tech</span> <span>6 min read</span></p>
      <ul class="mx-tags" aria-label="Tags"><li>#fixture</li></ul>
    </div>
  </header>
  <div class="mx-post-grid"><!-- Contents, then Prose --></div>
  <!-- Post foot -->
</article>
```

`.mx-post` is the Article page (04, "Patterns"): the masthead, then `.mx-post-grid` holding
Contents and the body, then the foot. On the blog's index the masthead has no path line, date or
tags: the title, then whatever the site puts in the slot (a meta line), and `.mx-index` follows.

## Variants and states

- Below 720px: no strip. From 720px: the strip, 100px wide, four strands (title, date and category,
  tags, file name).
- From 1100px on screen, on an article, the masthead and the foot span the contents rail and the body.
  On paper there is no rail: the masthead and the body are plain flow at the measure (05, "Print").
- The title is fluid, `font.size.title.min` to `font.size.title.max` (`--mx-text-title`), and balanced
  where `text-wrap: balance` is supported.
- Every context: the panel's face; path line and meta in `text-muted`, the current file and tags in
  `accent`, the title in `text-lead`.

## Behaviour

No element of its own. The strip is the Stream's strands and is drawn by `stream.css` and `rain.css`;
it stops with Hold rain and parks with reduced motion, as a stream does (05).

## Tokens

`color.accent`, `color.text-lead`, `color.text-muted`; `font.family.ja` (title), `font.family.mono`
(path line, tags); `font.size.title.min`, `font.size.title.max`, `font.size.meta`; `font.weight.medium`;
`font.leading.title`, `font.leading.ui`; `size.measure.read`, `size.measure.read-compact` and the
inset (`--mx-measure`, `--mx-inset` in `base.css`); `size.rail`; `space.0-5`, `space.1`, `space.1-5`,
`space.6`, `space.7`.

## Accessibility

The title is the page's one `h1`. The path line is a `nav` named Breadcrumb (パンくずリスト), its
`~` named Home and the file name `aria-current="page"`. Tags are a named list. The title, the
category or a tag in the other language carries `lang`. The strip is `aria-hidden`: every word in it
is in the masthead. Keyboard: the two path links, in order. Printed whole, without the strip (05, "Print").

## Do / Don't

- Do take the strip's words from the article itself.
- Don't put a second `h1` on an article.
- Don't draw the strip below 720px.

# Menu

## Purpose

Folds the nav and the controls into one native disclosure below 720px, so the header is one
slim row on a phone. From 720px up it lays no box at all.

## Contract

```html
<mx-menu>
  <details class="mx-menu">
    <summary class="mx-control"><span class="mx-menu-label">Menu</span></summary>
    <nav class="mx-nav" aria-label="Main">…</nav>
    <div class="mx-controls">…</div>
  </details>
</mx-menu>
```

## Variants and states

- From 720px: the `details` and its content are `display: contents`, the summary is not drawn,
  and the nav and controls are the header's own items whether it is open or closed.
- Below 720px, closed: a 46px button of three rules, in `text-muted`. Open (`[open]`): the
  filled `accent` face with one rule, and the nav and the controls unfold under the row as 44px
  lines.
- An engine without `::details-content` gets a plain disclosure labelled Menu at every width.

## Behaviour

The native `details` opens and closes without scripts. `mx-menu` adds four ways to close it:
Escape, a press outside the header, a change of reading (`mx:reading`) and `pagehide`. If focus
was on something that closing hides, it goes to the button. Nothing is missing without
JavaScript except those four.

## Tokens

`color.text-muted`, `color.accent`, `color.on-accent`, `color.rule`, `border.width.hair`,
`size.target`, `space.1`, `space.2`, `space.3`. The 46px cell, 3px row padding and the 16×12
three-rule glyph are the prototype's one-off numbers.

## Accessibility

A native disclosure: the summary is a button named by its (visually hidden) word, with its
expanded state. Keyboard: Tab to the button; Enter or Space opens; Tab moves through the nav
and controls; Escape closes and returns focus to the button.
In forced colours the three rules stay, in `ButtonText`; open, the button is `Highlight` and
its rule `HighlightText`.

## Do / Don't

- Do keep the markup order nav, then controls: it is the Tab order at every width.
- Don't add `aria-expanded` or `aria-controls`; the summary already exposes both.

# Meta

## Purpose

The small line of facts under an entry: its language, its date, its category.

## Contract

```html
<p class="mx-meta"><time datetime="2026-11-15">2026-11-15</time> Fixture</p>
```

## Variants and states

One: `meta` size, `text-muted`, tabular numerals.

## Behaviour

No element.

## Tokens

`color.text-muted`, `font.size.meta`, `space.1`.

## Accessibility

A paragraph; dates are `<time>`. `text-muted` at 13px measures 9.59:1 (Lc −61.1) in
phosphor-night, the value lifted by decision Q9.

## Do / Don't

- Do keep it to one line of facts.
- Don't make it smaller than `meta`.

# Moved

## Purpose

A stub page for an old address, because GitHub Pages cannot answer 301.

## Contract

```html
<!doctype html>
<html lang="en" data-theme="night">
  <head>
    <title>Moved | site</title>
    <link rel="canonical" href="https://example.com/to/">
    <script>location.replace(to + location.search + location.hash)</script>
    <meta http-equiv="refresh" content="0; url=/to/">
  </head>
  <body><main class="mx-frame mx-moved"><p>This page moved. <a href="/to/">/to/</a></p></main></body>
</html>
```

## Variants and states

One. The line sits 20% of the window down, on `ground`.

## Behaviour

With scripts the page replaces itself with the new address, carrying the query and the
fragment. Without scripts the refresh arrives without the query (05).

## Tokens

None beyond the base type; `20vh` is the prototype's one-off number.

## Accessibility

A page with one sentence and one link, in the page's language (`strings.moved`). It is
`noindex`; the canonical link names the new address.

## Do / Don't

- Do give the canonical as an absolute address.
- Don't add a delay to the refresh.

# Name

## Purpose

The page's one `h1`, shared by both readings (L3): giant and cut out of the site's own commit log in
人間用 (L1), a terminal line with a cursor in 機械用.

## Contract

```html
<h1 class="mx-name" id="name" style="--mx-etch:url(&quot;data:image/svg+xml,…&quot;)">wadakatu</h1>
```

`--mx-etch` is `nameMask(lines)` from `@wadakatu/matrix/lib`: an SVG mask with lines of commit
subjects and post titles cut out of it.

## Variants and states

- 人間用, from 720px: `--mx-text-display` (as wide as the frame), bold, `accent`, masked; the rain
  shows through the cuts (display type, the one place L2 allows it).
- 人間用, below 720px: solid, unmasked.
- 機械用: `--mx-text-prompt`, medium, no mask, a block cursor that blinks five times and rests lit,
  and phosphor bloom (`color.glow`, transparent by day).
- `data-double`: set by `mx-readings` for one 200ms frame when 人間用 returns.

## Behaviour

No element. `mx-readings` sets and clears `data-double`. Without scripts each reading's static route
shows its own drawing.

## Tokens

`color.accent`, `color.glow`, `color.rain.body`; `font.family.mono`, `font.weight.bold`,
`font.weight.medium`, `font.size.prompt.min`, `.max` (through `--mx-text-prompt`);
`motion.blink.duration`, `motion.blink.count`, `motion.double.duration`; `space.5`, `space.7`.

## Accessibility

One `h1` in every reading: it sits outside both reading containers, so it is never hidden. The mask
is an image and does not change the text. Reduced motion: the cursor is lit and does not blink; no
doubling.

## Do / Don't

- Do use it once per page with two readings.
- Don't put the mask over Japanese body text; it is for the name only.
- Don't add a glow by day: the token is transparent there on purpose.

# Nav

## Purpose

The site's main links in the header. The items are the site's; only the landmark's name is a
chrome string (L6).

## Contract

```html
<nav class="mx-nav" aria-label="Main">
  <a href="/" aria-current="page">Home</a>
  <a href="/projects/">Projects</a>
</nav>
```

## Variants and states

- 人間用: links in `text-muted`; the current one (`aria-current`) is `text-lead`, underlined
  2px in `accent`; hover is `text-lead`.
- 機械用 (`:root[data-reading="machine"]`): a numbered window list drawn with CSS counters,
  `0:Home*`, the current one starred in `accent` and not underlined. The numbers and the star
  are generated content with empty alternative text.
- Below 720px it is inside the Menu, as a column of 44px lines with dotted rules.

## Behaviour

No element.

## Tokens

`color.text-muted`, `color.text-lead`, `color.accent`, `border.width.strong`, `space.6`.

## Accessibility

A `nav` landmark named by the chrome string (`Main`, `メイン`). `aria-current="page"` on the
page itself, `"true"` within its section. Keyboard: Tab through the links in order.

## Do / Don't

- Do mark the current page with `aria-current`, never with a class.
- Don't put controls in the nav; they belong to the controls group.

tokens: [color.ground, color.panel, color.rule, color.text, color.text-lead, color.accent, color.focus, font.family.mono, font.family.ja, font.size.body, font.weight.regular, font.weight.medium, font.leading.ui, border.width.hair, border.width.strong, space.1, space.2, space.4, space.5, space.7, size.measure.lede, size.target-min]
---

# Notice

## Purpose

The 404 page and the offline page: one panel, no chrome, and nothing to fetch.

## Contract

```html
<!doctype html>
<html lang="en" data-theme="night">
  <head>
    <!-- Head: meta, the title, the pre-paint script, all inline -->
    <meta name="robots" content="noindex">
    <style>/* tokens.css, then notice.css */</style>
  </head>
  <body class="mx-notice">
    <main>
      <h1>Not found</h1>
      <p>Nothing is at this address.</p>
      <ul>
        <li><a href="/">Home</a></li>
        <li><a href="/blog/">Blog</a></li>
      </ul>
    </main>
  </body>
</html>
```

`Notice.astro` renders the whole document; give it `kind` (`not-found` or `offline`), `site`
(after the title) and `links` (label and address, the site's, as the footer's are), and
anything for the head in the `head` slot. `NoticeBody.astro` is the body alone, for the stories.

## Variants and states

- `not-found`: the title, the sentence and the site's links.
- `offline`: its own words, and "Try again" first: a link to the page's own address
  (`href=""`). The service worker serves this page at the address that failed, so following
  the link asks for it again.
- A link: hover takes `text-lead` and the strong underline; focus shows the ring.

## Behaviour

No script of its own. `tokens.css` and `notice.css` are inlined in one `style` element, and
`Head`'s script is inline, so the page requests nothing but itself; text falls to the system
faces at the end of `font.family.mono` and `font.family.ja`. A site that wants its fonts on the
404 page links `fonts.css` in the `head` slot; the offline page leaves it empty. The flags work
(`?theme=`, `?palette=`, a stored `mx-theme`); without scripts the page is night and phosphor.
It does not reload when the network comes back: the site keeps that beside its service worker
if it wants it.

`notice.css` repeats the few declarations of `base.css` the page needs (the ground, the body
type, the link and the focus ring), because the foundation files are not per-component
exports. `tests/matrix.spec.mjs` checks that the two copies compute the same in every context.

## Tokens

`color.ground`, `color.panel`, `color.rule`, `color.text`, `color.text-lead`, `color.accent`,
`color.focus`; `font.family.mono`, `font.family.ja`, `font.size.body`, `font.weight.regular`,
`font.weight.medium`, `font.leading.ui`; `border.width.hair`, `border.width.strong`; `space.1`,
`space.2`, `space.4`, `space.5`, `space.7`; `size.measure.lede`, `size.target-min`. The panel's
inline padding is the Panel's `clamp()`, and `20vh` is Moved's.

## Accessibility

One `main` with the page's one heading (`h1`), set as a panel's heading is. The words are chrome
strings in both languages (`strings.notice`). Keyboard: Tab goes through the links in order
("Try again" first when offline), each with the focus ring; nothing else takes focus. There is
no skip link, because there is one block. Each link is at least `size.target-min` tall. On
paper: the day ink, no fill, the border kept. Forced colours need no rule: the border and the
underlines stay. The page is `noindex`.

## Do / Don't

- Do serve the offline page from the service worker's precache, at the address that failed.
- Don't link a stylesheet, a font or an image on the offline page.
- Don't add chrome, rain or a script to either page.

# Panel

## Purpose

The solid surface reading text sits on, so that no paragraph is ever read over rain (L2).

## Contract

```html
<section class="mx-panel" aria-labelledby="activity">
  <h2 id="activity">Activity</h2>
  <p>…</p>
</section>
```

`aria-labelledby` and the heading's `id` are set only when `id` is given; a panel without a
heading is named with `label` (`aria-label`).

## Variants and states

None. In every context the face is `panel` with a 1px `rule` border; the heading is `accent`.

## Behaviour

No element. It is markup and CSS, and works without JavaScript.

## Tokens

`color.panel`, `color.rule`, `color.accent`; `font.size.body`, `font.weight.medium`,
`font.leading.ui` for the heading; `space.2`, `space.5`, `space.6`, `space.7`;
`border.width.hair`. The inline padding is the prototype's fluid `clamp(16px, 2.2vw, 28px)`.

## Accessibility

A `section`; a named region when it has an `id`. Its `h2` is the next level under the page's
`h1`. Nothing in it is focusable by itself.

## Do / Don't

- Do put every paragraph that is meant to be read on a panel or on `ground`.
- Don't make a panel transparent or translucent over rain (L2).
- Don't nest panels.
