# Post foot

## Purpose

The end of an article: the end-of-file line, Share, the older and newer posts, and the ways back to
both readings (L3).

## Contract

```html
<footer class="mx-postfoot mx-panel">
  <p class="mx-eof" aria-hidden="true">EOF</p>
  <mx-share class="mx-share">…</mx-share>
  <nav class="mx-pager" aria-label="Posts">
    <a href="/blog/b6e20d4f9a13c8/" rel="next"><span class="mx-pager-key">Newer</span><span>…</span></a>
  </nav>
  <p class="mx-ways">
    <a href="/blog/">All posts</a>
    <a href="/human/"><span lang="ja">人間用</span> Home</a>
    <a href="/?run=cat%20~/posts/3fa91c07d2b8e6.md"><span lang="ja">機械用</span>: <code>cat ~/posts/3fa91c07d2b8e6.md</code></a>
  </p>
</footer>
```

An older post is `rel="prev"`, a newer one `rel="next"`; the pager is left out when there is neither.

## Variants and states

- `EOF` in `text-muted`, spaced, with a block cursor in `accent` that does not blink.
- Pager: below 720px one column; from 720px two, the newer always in the second. Each a hairline box
  on `ground` (`accent` on hover), its key muted with `←` or `→`, the title in `text-lead`.
- From 1100px, on an article, it spans the contents rail and the body, as the masthead does.

## Behaviour

No element of its own; Share's is the only one. Everything else is links.

## Tokens

`color.accent`, `color.ground`, `color.rule`, `color.text-lead`, `color.text-muted`;
`font.family.mono`, `font.size.meta`, `font.size.body`, `font.leading.ui`; `border.width.hair`;
`size.measure.*`; `space.0-5`, `space.1-5`, `space.3`, `space.4`, `space.5`, `space.6`, `space.7`.

## Accessibility

A `footer` inside the `article`, so not the page's contentinfo. `EOF` is decoration and hidden. The
pager is a `nav` named Posts (記事); arrows are generated with empty alternative text. 人間用 and
機械用 carry `lang="ja"`. Keyboard: Share, the pager, the three ways back, in order. Not printed (05).

## Do / Don't

- Do link 機械用 to the shell at this file.
- Don't link a neighbour that leaves the site.
- Don't make the cursor blink.

<!-- Source: src/components/prompt/prompt.md -->

---
name: Prompt
status: approved
class: mx-prompt
attributes: []
tokens: [color.accent, color.on-accent, color.text-lead, font.size.read-compact, motion.blink.duration, motion.blink.count, space.1-5]
---

# Prompt

## Purpose

The command line: a real text field with the prompt before it and a drawn block cursor (L3).

## Contract

```html
<form class="mx-prompt" autocomplete="off">
  <label for="mx-command"><span class="mx-prompt-ps" aria-hidden="true"><span class="mx-prompt-who">fixture@example:~</span><span class="mx-prompt-sym">$</span></span><span class="mx-vh">Command</span></label>
  <span class="mx-prompt-field">
    <input id="mx-command" name="cmd" type="text" autocapitalize="off" autocorrect="off" spellcheck="false" enterkeyhint="go" aria-describedby="mx-command-hint" />
    <span class="mx-prompt-mirror" aria-hidden="true"></span><span class="mx-prompt-cursor" aria-hidden="true"> </span>
  </span>
</form>
<p class="mx-prompt-hint mx-vh" id="mx-command-hint">…</p>
```

## Variants and states

- Focused: the block is lit (`accent` under `on-accent`) and shows the character under the caret in
  reverse. Not focused: hollow, a 1px `accent` box. A selection hides it.
- Each keystroke starts five blinks (`motion.blink.*`), then it rests lit. Still: lit, no blink.
- Below 720px the path takes its own line and `$` starts the next. On coarse pointers the field is
  `font.size.read-compact` (16px), so iOS does not zoom into it.
- During a takeover or the rain overlay the prompt text is hidden; the field is the takeover's command line.

## Behaviour

`mx-terminal` owns it: Enter runs the line; Up and Down recall the history and bring the draft back;
Tab completes (asking the interpreter) only when the line has text and the caret is at its end, and
lists what is still ambiguous; Ctrl+L clears, Ctrl+C cancels the line, Ctrl+U cuts to the start,
Ctrl+A and Ctrl+E jump, Ctrl+D on an empty line exits; PageUp and PageDown scroll the session. Keys
are ignored while an input method composes. Without scripts the form is absent.

## Tokens

`color.accent`, `color.on-accent`, `color.text-lead`; `font.size.read-compact`; `motion.blink.duration`,
`motion.blink.count`; `space.1-5`.

## Accessibility

A labelled field (`Command`) described by a hint naming `help`, `exit`, the Tab rule and the Ctrl keys
it takes. Tab is never a trap: on an empty line, with Shift, or after Escape it moves focus. Ctrl+C is
left to the browser while text is selected, so copying works on Windows and Linux. The block cursor
replaces the 2px ring (05, "Focus"): lit with focus, hollow without. Forced colours: `Highlight`.

## Do / Don't

- Do keep the field a real `<input>`.
- Don't take Ctrl keys while the field does not have focus.
- Don't focus the field on arrival on touch devices.

tokens: [color.accent, color.ground, color.rule, color.text, color.text-lead, color.text-muted, font.family.ja, font.family.mono, font.size.read, font.size.read-compact, font.size.heading, font.size.lead, font.size.body, font.size.label, font.size.meta, font.weight.medium, font.weight.regular, font.leading.read, font.leading.ui, border.width.hair, border.width.strong, radius.control, size.measure.read, size.measure.read-compact, space.2, space.3, space.5, space.7]
---

# Prose

## Purpose

Long-form reading, tuned for Japanese, on one solid panel (L2). Everything a Markdown renderer can
emit is styled. The core is approved; the table, the task list and the footnotes are drafts (04).

## Contract

```html
<div class="mx-prose mx-panel">
  <h2 id="intro">…</h2>
  <p>… <code>inline</code> … <strong>…</strong> … <a href="https://example.com/">…</a></p>
  <ul><li>…</li></ul>
</div>
```

The drafts, inside the same panel (04, "Reading drafts"):

```html
<div class="mx-table" role="group" aria-label="Table" tabindex="0"><table>…</table></div>
<ul class="contains-task-list"><li class="task-list-item"><label><input type="checkbox" disabled checked> …</label></li></ul>
<p>…<sup><a href="#user-content-fn-1" id="user-content-fnref-1" data-footnote-ref aria-describedby="footnote-label">1</a></sup></p>
<section data-footnotes class="footnotes">
  <h2 class="sr-only" id="footnote-label">Footnotes</h2>
  <ol><li id="user-content-fn-1"><p>… <a href="#user-content-fnref-1" data-footnote-backref aria-label="Back to reference 1">↩</a></p></li></ol>
</section>
```

The body is the site's Markdown rendering (01); `Prose.astro` is the panel around it and `Table.astro`
the table's wrapper. Code blocks, Reference links, callouts and details have their own pages.

## Variants and states

| Element | Setting |
| --- | --- |
| Body | `font.family.ja`; `read-compact` below 720px, `read` from 720px, `leading.read`; the measure, 40 full-width characters (`size.measure.*`); `line-break: strict`; no justification |
| `h2`, `h3`, `h4` | `heading` / `lead` / body size; `##` before each, generated, seen and not read |
| Links, `strong` | Underlined `accent`; medium `text-lead` |
| Lists | `-` and numbers in `accent`, mono |
| `hr`, `blockquote` | A dashed `rule`; a 2px `rule` at the left, muted text |
| Inline code | `ground`, a hairline `rule`, `text-lead`, 0.9em (`--mx-text-code`) |
| Images | The real file in a hairline `rule`, never recoloured |
| Table (draft) | Scrolls in `.mx-table`; head `text-muted`, a solid hairline under it, dotted between rows |
| Task list (draft) | `[x]` / `[ ]` in place of `-`; the checkbox visually hidden; done items neither struck nor dimmed |
| Footnotes (draft) | `[1]` references in mono, a dashed rule before the section, `↩` back (underlined, as any link: without it axe's `link-in-text-block` fails), the target marked by a 2px `accent` rule and `text-lead` |

Characters per line measured on the Article specimens: 20.6 at 390, 38.4 at 768, 38.1 at 1100,
39.9 at 1440, the prototype's four figures.

## Behaviour

No element. Static HTML and CSS; complete without scripts. In print: dark ink on white, absolute
`http(s)` links followed by their address, no back references, break rules (05, "Print").

## Tokens

`color.accent`, `color.ground`, `color.rule`, `color.text`, `color.text-lead`, `color.text-muted`;
`font.family.ja`, `font.family.mono`; `font.size.read`, `font.size.read-compact`, `font.size.heading`,
`font.size.lead`, `font.size.body`, `font.size.label`, `font.size.meta`; `font.weight.medium`,
`font.weight.regular`; `font.leading.read`, `font.leading.ui`; `border.width.hair`,
`border.width.strong`; `radius.control`; `size.measure.*` (`--mx-measure`, `--mx-inset`); `space.2`,
`space.3`, `space.5`, `space.7`.

## Accessibility

Headings in order under the masthead's `h1`; markers and list numbers generated with empty
alternative text. Images carry the author's `alt`; Prose never invents one. A table's wrapper is a
labelled group (`Table` / `表`) and one tab stop, so it scrolls from the keyboard. A task item's
checkbox keeps its role, state and name through its `label`; it is disabled, so not a tab stop. The
footnote heading stays in the page, hidden, for the references' `aria-describedby`.

## Do / Don't

- Do keep reading text on this panel (L2).
- Don't justify Japanese or tighten its tracking.
- Don't drop the table's wrapper: without it the table cannot scroll.

<!-- Source: src/effects/rain/rain.md -->

---
name: Rain
status: approved
class: mx-rain
attributes: [data-variant, data-rain, data-motion]
tokens: [color.rain.tail, color.rain.body, color.rain.head, color.ground, font.family.dot, font.size.rain, layer.rain]
---

# Rain

## Purpose

The ambient rain behind 人間用: columns of drops, each drop a piece of one of the site's own phrases
(L1). It shows only in the gaps, the margins and behind the giant name (L2).

## Contract

```html
<div class="mx-rain" aria-hidden="true">
  <span class="mx-rain-col" style="--x:1.25%">
    <span class="mx-drop" lang="ja" style="--t:14.2s;--d:-3.1s;--rest:31%">見本の局を追加</span>
  </span>
</div>
```

Generated at build time by `rainColumns(phrases)` from `@wadakatu/matrix/lib`: 40 columns × 3 drops,
up to 20 glyphs a drop, Japanese and Latin phrases alternating, one speed per column between
`motion.rain.duration.min` and `.max`, seeded so every build is identical. `--rest` is the drop's
place in the still.

## Variants and states

- Default: fixed to the window, behind everything (`layer.rain`). Every second column is hidden
  below 1100px, three of four below 720px.
- `data-variant="band"` (blog): one viewport tall, not fixed, fading out from half way, so it
  scrolls away when reading starts.
- Held (`:has()` on the Hold rain checkbox, or `data-rain="held"`): every drop paused.
- Still (`data-motion="off"` or reduced motion): drops parked at `--rest` down the whole document;
  the layer scrolls with the page; the Hold control is hidden.
- 機械用: not drawn.
- Each drop is a gradient clipped to its text (`rain.tail` → `rain.body` → `rain.head`), the same
  roles in all four contexts.

## Behaviour

CSS only: one transform animation per drop (`mx-drop-vh`), with plain units in the keyframes so a
palette or theme change while held never re-resolves the paused drops (the prototype's freeze).
Works without scripts, held included.

## Tokens

`color.rain.tail`, `color.rain.body`, `color.rain.head`, `color.ground` (the band's mask);
`font.family.dot`, `font.size.rain`; `layer.rain`. The columns' falls are `rainColumns` in `lib`,
whose 9s and 21s defaults are the values of `motion.rain.duration.min` and `.max`; no file reads the
tokens.

## Accessibility

`aria-hidden`: the same facts are readable on the page. Hold rain (05, "One switch for all endless
motion") stops it in both readings; reduced motion parks it. Not drawn in forced colours. No more
than 170 animating elements on a page, rain included (05, "Performance").

## Do / Don't

- Do feed it the site's own phrases; the film-name filter runs inside the helper.
- Don't put reading text over it: reading text sits on a Panel.
- Don't animate drops with custom properties in keyframes.

<!-- Source: src/components/readings/readings.md -->

---
name: Readings
status: approved
element: mx-readings
attributes: [data-reading, aria-busy]
tokens: [font.size.ui, font.leading.terminal, space.1]
---

# Readings

## Purpose

Both readings of one page in one document, and the in-place change between them (L3).

## Contract

```html
<mx-readings data-human-title="…" data-machine-title="…" data-human-status="Human reading" data-machine-status="Machine reading">
  <h1 class="mx-name">wadakatu</h1>
  <div data-reading="human">…</div>
  <div data-reading="machine">…</div>
</mx-readings>
```

Links that lead to a reading carry `data-to="human|machine"` (the Switch, the guide's link, the status
line's link). Links that follow the reading carry both addresses: `data-human-href` and
`data-machine-href` (the Mark, the Nav, a panel's links).

## Variants and states

- The root's `data-reading` decides which child is shown; the other is `display: none`.
- `aria-busy="true"` while a change runs.
- 機械用's container is set at `font.size.ui` on `font.leading.terminal`.

## Behaviour

`mx-readings` turns a click on any `a[data-to]`, or the `\` / `¥` shortcut, into an in-place change:
the root attribute, the address (the static twin with the carried flags: `palette`, `motion`), the
title, "Machine reading" / "Human reading" in the status region, `aria-current` on the switches, the
links that follow the reading, and focus, moved to the header switch if it was inside the reading
being hidden. It emits `mx:reading` with the new value (again when the session has printed).

With motion: into 機械用 the text on screen turns into the hex of its own characters, the picture
collapses to a line, and the session prints; back, the session clears from the bottom, the page opens
from a line, its headings settle and the Name doubles once. Web Animations API, no third-party code
(decision Q6, spike S3). A second request finishes the first, completely, then starts; reduced motion
switched on mid-change finishes it; leaving the page finishes it. Nothing is left styled, scrambled or
`aria-busy`.

The shortcut has the prototype's guards (modifiers except AltGr, form fields, editable content, IME
composition, already-handled events, the boot) and an off switch: the "Enable `\` / `¥` shortcut"
checkbox, stored as `localStorage['mx-shortcut']`, in the footer and in the menu (from 720px the
menu shows it only in the live shell, where the footer is gone).

Without scripts every `a[data-to]` is a plain link to its static twin and the shortcut and its off
switch are absent.

## Tokens

`font.size.ui`, `font.leading.terminal`; `space.1`.

## Accessibility

The hidden reading is out of the accessibility tree and the tab order. One polite announcement per
change. Focus is never left in a hidden reading. The shortcut can be turned off (2.1.4) from both
readings. Reduced motion: an instant change.

## Do / Don't

- Do give both readings the same facts (L3).
- Don't put the Name inside one reading.
- Don't link a reading with `data-reading`; that attribute is for the containers.

<!-- Source: src/components/ref/ref.md -->

name: Reference link
status: approved

tokens: [color.accent, color.ground, color.rule, color.text-lead, color.text-muted, font.family.mono, font.size.meta, font.leading.ui, border.width.hair, border.width.strong, space.2, space.3]
---

# Reference link

## Purpose

A link whose text is its own address, written alone on a line: host, then path, so the reader sees
where it goes (L1).

## Contract

```html
<a class="mx-ref" href="https://example.com/fixture/station/README.md"><span class="mx-ref-host">example.com</span><span class="mx-ref-path">/fixture/station/README.md</span></a>
```

`Ref.astro` takes the absolute address and splits it; a leading `www.` is not shown.

## Variants and states

One. `ground` cut into the panel, a hairline `rule` with a 2px `accent` rule at the left, `↗` in
`accent`; host `text-lead`, path `text-muted`, mono at `meta` size, wrapping anywhere. Hover: the
border goes `accent` and the host is underlined.

## Behaviour

No element. A plain link.

## Tokens

`color.accent`, `color.ground`, `color.rule`, `color.text-lead`, `color.text-muted`;
`font.family.mono`, `font.size.meta`, `font.leading.ui`; `border.width.hair`, `border.width.strong`;
`space.2`, `space.3`.

## Accessibility

Named by its address. The arrow is generated with empty alternative text. Focus: the 2px ring. In
print it is not followed by its address again (05).

## Do / Don't

- Do use it only for a link whose text is its address.
- Don't shorten the path.
- Don't put words of your own in it.

name: Rewards
status: approved
class: mx-ghost
attributes: [data-reward, data-double]
tokens: [color.panel, color.accent, motion.echo.duration, space.1]
---

# Rewards

## Purpose

Three small one-shot effects made of the site's own material (L1): déjà vu, a title turning into the
commit that shipped it, and the Name doubling. Decode is the text effect they and the change share.

## Contract

```html
<li class="mx-stream" data-commit="feat(fixture-one): …" data-reward="flick">
  …<h3 class="mx-stream-name" data-echo="fixture-one"><a href="…">fixture-one</a>
     <span class="mx-ghost" aria-hidden="true"><span lang="en">feat(fixture-one): …</span></span></h3>…
</li>
```

`data-echo`, `data-commit` are in the Stream's markup; `data-reward` and `.mx-ghost` are added and
removed by the script.

## Variants and states

- Déjà vu (`data-reward="deja"`): the second time a reader points at or focuses an entry, its name
  repeats once over itself, `motion.echo.duration`.
- Title to commit (`data-reward="flick"`): once, about two seconds after an entry with a commit is
  first fully on screen, its title decodes into the commit and back.
- The name doubles (`data-double` on the Name, `motion.double.duration`) on the way back to 人間用.
- Decode: text settles out of the corpus's glyph pools (`decodeFrame` in `lib`; `<mx-root
  data-wide data-narrow>` from the Layout's `corpus`), `motion.decode.duration` for headings and the
  switch side just taken.

## Behaviour

`effects/rewards/rewards.ts` (loaded with the elements) delegates from the document. Every reward is
off with reduced motion and while rain is held; turning either on mid-reward, changing reading, or
leaving the page removes what it added.

## Tokens

`color.panel`, `color.accent`; `motion.echo.duration`; `space.1`. The doubling reads
`motion.double.duration` and `color.rain.body` in Name's stylesheet. Title to commit decodes for
300ms and 250ms, numbers in `rewards.ts`; headings and the switch side decode for 450ms, the value of
`motion.decode.duration`, a number in `mx-readings.ts`. No file reads that token.

## Accessibility

Every overlay is `aria-hidden` or generated content with empty alternative text; the link keeps its
name. Glyph shapes change at constant ink colour, never a luminance pulse (05, "Flashing").

## Do / Don't

- Do pair a title with a commit only when the commit is really in the log.
- Don't add a reward that repeats.

<!-- Source: src/components/root/root.md -->

---
name: Root
status: approved
element: mx-root
attributes: [data-theme, data-palette, data-motion, data-rain]
tokens: []
---

# Root

## Purpose

The controller of the page's state: theme, palette, motion and the flags in-site links carry, kept in
step with the attributes the head script set before the first paint (L7).

## Contract

```html
<mx-root data-wide="…" data-narrow="…">…the page…</mx-root>
```

Rendered by Layout around the whole body. `data-wide` and `data-narrow` are the corpus's glyph pools,
which Decode reads (L1). The controls it drives are Control's: `[data-action="theme"]`,
`[data-action="palette"]` and `[data-action="hold"] input`.

## Variants and states

What it keeps on `<html>`:

- `data-theme`: `day` or `night`, flipped by Daylight and stored as `localStorage['mx-theme']`.
- `data-palette="operator"`: set and removed by Operator colours, which rewrites the address; never
  stored (decision Q4).
- `data-motion="off"`: follows the system's reduced-motion setting live, and stays off for `?motion=0`.
- `data-rain="held"`: while Hold rain is checked.

## Behaviour

On connection it removes TOMBO's old `tombo-theme` key, wires the three controls and syncs: each
toggle's `aria-pressed`, `theme-color` from the root's background, and every in-site link, which
carries `palette=operator` exactly while the palette is on and `motion=0` exactly while the address
has it. Changing the palette also drops the spent flags from the address. `carry()` and `sync()` are
public; Readings uses them. Storage that throws changes nothing visible. Without it
the head script still carries the flags on links, and the theme and palette toggles are hidden
(Control).

## Tokens

None. `display: block` is its only style.

## Accessibility

The toggles' pressed state is `aria-pressed`, always in step with the root. It adds no focusable
element and moves no focus.

## Do / Don't

- Do keep one `<mx-root>` per page, around everything.
- Don't store the palette or the motion flag.

# Run

## Purpose

A command in output that can be tapped to run: a file name in a listing, a suggestion in a message (L3).

## Contract

```html
<button class="mx-run" type="button" tabindex="-1" data-run="help">help</button>
```

## Variants and states

`accent` text, underlined on hover. With the `dir` tone it is `text-lead`, medium.

## Behaviour

`mx-terminal` runs `data-run` on a click or tap without moving focus. Printed by `render` from a run
segment (`{ text, run }`). Without scripts it is still a button, because the recorded and live output
are one markup (4.1); it is styled as text and does nothing.

## Tokens

`color.accent`.

## Accessibility

A button outside the tab order, so a listing does not add a tab stop per file name; everything a run
does can also be typed. Inline in a line of output, so the target-size exception for inline targets
applies (2.5.8).

## Do / Don't

- Do run exactly what it says.
- Don't put it in the tab order.
- Don't make what a reader typed into a run.

# Scan lines

## Purpose

The tube in 機械用: a fixed wash of `color.scanline` on one pixel row in three, over the whole screen.

## Contract

```html
<!-- A root effect: no markup. `:root[data-reading="machine"] body::after` -->
```

## Variants and states

- 機械用 only. Under the status line (`layer.scanline` 20 < `layer.status` 25).
- The logo, the header switch, the open menu button and pressed controls are lifted above them
  (`layer.lifted`), so the mark is shown as designed (L5) and filled faces keep their glyphs.
- Not drawn in forced colours or in print.

## Behaviour

CSS only; no pointer events.

## Tokens

`color.scanline`; `layer.scanline`, `layer.lifted`. It sits under `layer.status`, which the status
line reads.

## Accessibility

Contrast is measured without them; the night margins absorb the 28% wash (05, rule 7).

## Do / Don't

- Do lift anything filled with `accent` in 機械用.
- Don't draw them in 人間用.

# Share

## Purpose

Ways to pass an article on: Post on X, Copy link, and the system's share sheet where there is one.

## Contract

```html
<mx-share class="mx-share" data-url="https://example.com/blog/3fa91c07d2b8e6/" data-title="…" data-copied="Copied" data-failed="Not copied">
  <span class="mx-share-label">Share</span>
  <a class="mx-control" href="https://x.com/intent/post?text=…&amp;url=…" rel="noopener">Post on X</a>
  <button class="mx-control" type="button" data-share="link">Copy link</button>
  <button class="mx-control" type="button" data-share="sheet" hidden>Share…</button>
</mx-share>
```

`data-url` is the article's canonical address, the one shared and copied.

## Variants and states

- Without scripts: the label and Post on X only.
- With scripts: Copy link, which says Copied (or Not copied) for 1.6s.
- With scripts and `navigator.share`: Share… as well. Nowhere else is it shown.
- The controls are Control's look at `meta` size.

## Behaviour

`mx-share` copies `data-url`, and unhides the sheet button only where `navigator.share` exists; a
dismissed sheet is not an error. Post on X is a plain link and needs nothing.

## Tokens

`color.text-muted`, `font.size.meta`, `space.2`; the controls read Control's tokens.

## Accessibility

A link and two buttons, each named by its word; the label is text before them. No dead button
without scripts (05). Keyboard: Tab through them; Enter or Space presses. Not printed (part of the
post foot).

## Do / Don't

- Do share the canonical address.
- Don't show the sheet button where `navigator.share` is missing.
- Don't load a third party's script for it.

# Status

## Purpose

The page's one polite live region, where a change of reading is announced (L3).

## Contract

```html
<p class="mx-status mx-vh" role="status"></p>
```

## Variants and states

None. It is visually hidden in every context.

## Behaviour

Empty in the markup. `mx-readings` (task 3.6) writes `Machine reading` or `Human reading` into
it, in the page's language (`strings.status`). Without scripts nothing changes in place, so
nothing is announced.

## Tokens

None; it uses the `.mx-vh` utility.

## Accessibility

`role="status"`: polite, atomic. One per page, rendered by the Layout.

## Do / Don't

- Do write to it only when something changed in place.
- Don't add a second live region for the same purpose.

# Status line

## Purpose

tmux's status line for 機械用: the reading, where the shell is, the time in Japan, and the way back (L3).

## Contract

```html
<p class="mx-modeline">
  <span class="mx-modeline-mode">[<span lang="ja">機械用</span>]</span>
  <span class="mx-modeline-where">recorded session</span>
  <span class="mx-modeline-time"></span>
  <a class="mx-modeline-way" data-to="human" href="/human/"><span lang="ja">人間用</span></a>
</p>
```

## Variants and states

- Recorded: `recorded session`, no time; fixed to the bottom of the scrolling page.
- Live: `0:sh* ~` (process, working directory), the time as `HH:MM JST`; a row of the one viewport.
  The process becomes the takeover's name, or `rain` with how to stop it.
- Hidden while an on-screen keyboard is up. `accent` fill in all four contexts; it stays above the
  scan lines (`layer.status`).

## Behaviour

`mx-terminal` writes the process, the directory and the clock (every 20 seconds). The link is an
`a[data-to="human"]`: the in-place change with `mx-readings`, a plain link without it.

## Tokens

`color.accent`, `color.on-accent`; `font.size.meta`, `font.weight.medium`; `layer.status`; `space.1`.

## Accessibility

A paragraph; the arrow before the link is generated content with empty alternative text. Focus on the
filled face: the ring is drawn in `on-accent` (05, "Focus"). Forced colours: `Highlight` /
`HighlightText`.

## Do / Don't

- Do keep the way back on screen in 機械用.
- Don't put reading text in it.
- Don't let the scan lines cross it.

<!-- Source: src/components/stream/stream.md -->

---
name: Stream
status: approved
class: mx-stream
attributes: []
tokens: [color.rule, color.text-lead, color.accent, color.focus, font.family.mono, font.family.ja, font.size.body, font.size.ui, font.weight.medium, font.size.rain, border.width.hair, border.width.strong, space.2, space.3, space.4]
---

# Stream

## Purpose

One entry of the wall: strands of its own words fall beside (or above) its readable text, and settle
into it (L1, L2).

## Contract

```html
<li class="mx-stream" data-commit="feat: …">
  <div class="mx-stream-fall" aria-hidden="true">
    <span class="mx-strand" style="--j:0"><span class="mx-drop" style="--t:7.3s;--d:-2.1s;--rest:20%">fixture-on</span></span>
  </div>
  <div class="mx-stream-entry">
    <h3 class="mx-stream-name" data-echo="fixture-one"><a href="…">fixture-one</a></h3>
    <p class="mx-meta">TypeScript</p>
    <p class="mx-blurb">A fixture tool…</p>
  </div>
</li>
```

Strands come from `streamStrands(texts, index)`: two short drops of each text, half a cycle apart, one
speed per strand between `motion.strand.duration.min` and `.max`. `data-commit` is a commit that
shipped the entry, for the title-to-commit reward (Rewards).

## Variants and states

- Beside its entry (default); above it in the wall from 1360px (Streams). Three strands, four in
  rows from 720px and in the wall.
- Hover or focus inside: the strands pause and come up to `accent`; the name is underlined.
- Held: paused. Still: one parked drop per strand.
- `level`: `h3` on Home, `h2` on Projects.

## Behaviour

CSS only. The rewards (déjà vu, title to commit) attach to it without markup of their own.

## Tokens

`color.rule`, `color.text-lead`, `color.accent`, `color.focus`;
`font.family.mono`, `font.family.ja`, `font.size.body`, `font.size.ui`, `font.weight.medium`,
`font.size.rain`; `border.width.hair`, `border.width.strong`; `space.2`, `space.3`, `space.4`. On hover
or focus it sets `--mx-color-rain-body` and `--mx-color-rain-tail` to the accent for Rain's drop
style to read. The strands' falls are `streamStrands` in `lib`, whose 5s and 11s defaults are the
values of `motion.strand.duration.min` and `.max`; no file reads the tokens.

## Accessibility

The strands are `aria-hidden`; the entry is real text and a link. When the link has focus the whole
stream is outlined instead of the link (05, "Focus"). Keyboard: Tab to the name's link, then to any
link in the entry.

## Do / Don't

- Do give the strands the entry's own texts (name, line, host, language or date).
- Don't make the whole entry one link.
- Don't put a strand over the entry's text.

<!-- Source: src/components/streams/streams.md -->

---
name: Streams
status: approved
class: mx-streams
attributes: [data-variant]
tokens: [color.rule, color.accent, border.width.hair, font.size.entry.min, font.size.entry.max, font.size.body, font.leading.tight, space.3, space.4, space.5, space.6]
---

# Streams

## Purpose

The list of Streams: a wall on Home, rows on Projects (L1).

## Contract

```html
<ul class="mx-streams">
  <li class="mx-stream">…</li>
</ul>
<ul class="mx-streams" data-variant="rows">…</ul>
```

## Variants and states

- Default (the wall): stacked below 1360px; from 1360px seven columns, each stream falling into its
  entry from above; the entry's top rule lights `accent` on hover and focus.
- `data-variant="rows"`: always stacked; names at `--mx-text-entry` in `accent`; four strands and
  more room from 720px.

## Behaviour

CSS only.

## Tokens

`color.rule`, `color.accent`; `border.width.hair`; `font.size.entry.min`, `.max` (through
`--mx-text-entry`), `font.size.body`, `font.leading.tight`; `space.3`, `space.4`, `space.5`, `space.6`.

## Accessibility

A list. Keyboard order is the reading order of the entries, in both arrangements.

## Do / Don't

- Do use the wall for a mix of projects and posts, rows for one kind.
- Don't set a column count of your own.

# Swatches

## Purpose

The eight theme colours of the context, as neofetch shows a terminal's colours (L7).

## Contract

```html
<span class="mx-swatches" aria-hidden="true">
  <span class="mx-swatch" data-swatch="panel"></span>
  <span class="mx-swatch" data-swatch="accent"></span>
</span>
```

All eight, in this order: `panel`, `rule`, `rain-tail`, `rain-body`, `muted`, `text`, `lead`, `accent`.

## Variants and states

One cell per role, 3ch by 1.2em, in all four contexts; each cell reads its role, so it follows the context.

## Behaviour

Printed by `render` from the segment `{ swatches: true }`. No behaviour.

## Tokens

`color.panel`, `color.rule`, `color.rain.tail`, `color.rain.body`, `color.text-muted`, `color.text`,
`color.text-lead`, `color.accent`.

## Accessibility

Decoration: `aria-hidden`. Forced colours keep the fills, since they are the content.

## Do / Don't

- Do keep the order.
- Don't use a swatch as a control.
- Don't name a hue.

tokens: [color.ground, color.panel, color.text, color.text-muted, color.text-lead, color.accent, color.on-accent, color.rain.head, color.control-border, color.reading.human, color.reading.machine, font.family.dot, font.family.mono, font.size.rain, font.size.meta, font.size.label, font.leading.ui, radius.control, radius.capsule, border.width.hair, size.target, motion.drip.duration, motion.wipe.duration, motion.wipe.steps, space.3, space.5]
---

# Switch

## Purpose

The choice between the two readings (L3): two real links to the two static routes, so it works
without scripts. `mx-readings` makes the change happen in place.

## Contract

```html
<mx-switch class="mx-switch" role="group" aria-label="Reading">
  <a class="mx-switch-side" data-to="human" href="/human/" aria-current="true">
    <span class="mx-switch-label" lang="ja">人間用</span>
  </a>
  <a class="mx-switch-side" data-to="machine" href="/">
    <span class="mx-switch-label" lang="ja">機械用</span>
  </a>
</mx-switch>
```

The capsule adds `data-variant="capsule"` and a `<small>` note after each label.

## Variants and states

- `rain` (default; the header and the boot layer): each name a strand, upright vertical text in
  `font.family.dot`. The current side is filled `accent` with `on-accent`, wiped in from the top
  (`motion.wipe.*`). A drop falls through the idle side every `motion.drip.duration`; hover stops it.
- `rain` at most 600px wide, in the header: one 44×44 button showing the current reading; a hole
  travels down it and shows the other name.
- `capsule` ("Two readings" on 人間用 Home): a large capsule, a note under each name, and a dot in
  `color.reading.*` beside each.
- On the boot layer neither side is current, and both drip half a cycle apart.
- Still: no drop, no wipe; the idle label is plain `text-muted`; the compact button shows `▾`.
- `brace` and `bits` are not drawings of matrix (decision Q5), and there is no `?switch=` flag.

## Behaviour

`mx-switch` keeps the compact button one tab stop: the current side is `aria-hidden` and out of the
tab order, the other is named by its destination (`人間用から機械用へ`), and focus follows when the
pressed face hides. Without scripts the two links are both in the tab order and both work.

## Tokens

`color.ground`, `color.panel`, `color.text`, `color.text-muted`, `color.text-lead`, `color.accent`,
`color.on-accent`, `color.rain.head`, `color.control-border`, `color.reading.human`,
`color.reading.machine`; `font.family.dot`, `font.family.mono`, `font.size.rain`, `font.size.meta`,
`font.size.label`, `font.leading.ui`; `radius.control`, `radius.capsule`; `border.width.hair`;
`size.target`; `motion.drip.duration`, `motion.wipe.duration`, `motion.wipe.steps`; `space.3`, `space.5`.

## Accessibility

A group named "Reading" (表示 in Japanese) of two links named 人間用 and 機械用, `lang="ja"` (names,
never glossed). `aria-current="true"` marks the side shown; colour is never the only signal. Focus:
the 2px ring with a 2px `ground` gap inside it, so it shows on the filled face (C40). Keyboard: Tab
to each side, Enter changes reading; `\` / `¥` when the shortcut is on (`aria-keyshortcuts`).
Forced colours: the current side is `Highlight` / `HighlightText`, the idle label gets its colour back.
Hold rain stops the drop in both readings (05).

## Do / Don't

- Do link each side to its static twin.
- Don't add a third drawing or a flag to choose one.
- Don't use the dots without the names beside them.

<!-- Source: src/components/takeover/takeover.md -->

---
name: Takeover
status: approved
class: mx-takeover
attributes: []
tokens: [color.text-muted, color.text-lead]
---

# Takeover

## Purpose

A full-screen view inside the screen whose command line is the prompt: the site's `vim` (L3).

## Contract

```html
<div class="mx-takeover" hidden>
  <pre class="mx-takeover-buffer">…<span data-tone="dim">~</span></pre>
  <p class="mx-takeover-message" role="status"></p>
</div>
```

## Variants and states

- Hidden (the default) or open: the buffer, a column of tildes in `text-muted`, and a message line in
  `text-lead`. While it is open the session is hidden and the prompt text is gone; the field is its
  command line. The status line shows the takeover's process name.

## Behaviour

An interpreter opens it with the effect `takeover: { name, lines, message, announce }`, updates it the
same way, and closes it with `takeover: null`. While it is open, Enter passes the line to `exec`;
keys typed outside a `:` command line, Escape and Ctrl+C go to the interpreter's `key()` at once.
Absent without scripts.

## Tokens

`color.text-muted`, `color.text-lead`.

## Accessibility

When it opens, `announce` (how to leave) is said in the page's status region; its message line is a
status. Keyboard: the field keeps focus throughout.

## Do / Don't

- Do say how to leave when it opens.
- Don't trap the reader: Tab still moves focus.
- Don't open it without a command.

---
name: Terminal

class: mx-terminal
element: mx-terminal
attributes: [data-shell, data-keyboard, data-zoom, data-overlay, data-tone]
tokens: [color.text-muted, color.text-lead, color.accent, color.panel, color.ground, color.rule, font.size.ui, font.leading.terminal, font.weight.medium, space.1-5, space.3, space.4, space.6, layer.overlay]
---

# Terminal

## Purpose

機械用 as one shell in one viewport: the same facts as 人間用, typed for and printed as a session (L3).
Without scripts it is a recorded session in an ordinary scrolling page.

## Contract

```html
<mx-terminal class="mx-terminal" data-cwd="~" data-first="neofetch" data-login="fixture_, Fixture developer">
  <p class="mx-guide">…</p>
  <div class="mx-terminal-screen" tabindex="0" role="group" aria-label="Terminal">
    <div class="mx-terminal-tty">
      <div class="mx-ln"><span data-tone="dim">…</span></div>
      <div class="mx-ln mx-ln-echo"><span class="mx-prompt-ps" aria-hidden="true">fixture@example:~$</span> ls</div>
    </div>
    <div class="mx-takeover" hidden>…</div>
    <form class="mx-prompt" autocomplete="off">…</form>
    <p class="mx-prompt-hint mx-vh" id="mx-command-hint">…</p>
  </div>
  <div class="mx-chips" role="group" aria-label="Keys and suggested commands">…</div>
  <p class="mx-modeline">…</p>
</mx-terminal>
```

`Terminal.astro` takes the site's `interpreter`, the recorded `session` (its commands; the first is the
login command), the `chips`, the way back (`human`), `login` (who the login card is about) and `lang`.
It runs the interpreter at build time and prints with `render` from `@wadakatu/matrix/lib`, the same
function the element prints live output with, so the two are the same markup.

The interpreter contract (04) is in `lib`: `prompt()` (user, host, working directory, process name),
`motd()`, `exec(line)` returning `{ out, fx }`, `complete(line)` returning candidates for the last
word, and `key(k)` for keys while a takeover is open. An item is a line of segments (text, a tone, a
link, a run, the swatches) or a card (an image with lines beside it). Effects: `open`, `exit`, `clear`,
`theme`, `palette`, `takeover`, `overlay: "rain"`, `navigate`; unknown ones are ignored.

## Variants and states

- Recorded (no attribute on the root; `data-shell="recorded"` after the fallback): the session as a
  scrolling page; the prompt, chips, the guide's × and the clock are absent; the status line, fixed to
  the bottom, says `recorded session`.
- Live (`<html data-shell="live">`): the element printed a fresh session and the prompt waits. In
  機械用 the page is one viewport: header, guide, screen, chips, status line; the session scrolls
  inside the screen. The name (`h1`) is visually hidden and the footer is gone.
- `data-keyboard` on the element (an on-screen keyboard is up): the status line and guide give way,
  and from 720px the window list too.
- `data-zoom` on the element (a pinch zoom leaves under 480 visible CSS px, no keyboard): the one
  viewport lets go and the document scrolls.
- `data-overlay="rain"`: the page's own rain over the window until any key; parked still with motion off.
- Below 1360px in the live shell, the Operator and Daylight buttons give way to `theme` and
  `palette`, so that the shortcut's off switch fits the one header row (69px at 1100); below 720px
  as in the prototype. An interpreter for this terminal offers both commands.
- All four contexts read roles only; the output's tones are `dim` (muted), `hi` (accent), `dir` (lead).

## Behaviour

`mx-terminal` goes live when the site gives it an interpreter (`element.interpreter = …`). It prints
`motd()`, then the login command (as the login card when `data-login` is set) or `?run=` instead,
neither of which enters the history; sets `role="log"` on the session after that first screen; sets
`<html data-shell="live">`; and focuses the field on fine pointers only. The line editor, the keys and
the cursor are the Prompt's. Effects: `open` only with a user gesture (`?run=` prints the link only);
`theme` and `palette` press the header's controls; `exit` follows the header's 人間用 link, so the
change is the page's own; `navigate` keeps the carried flags; `clear` empties the session.

The viewport: with scripts running, 機械用 is locked to one viewport whose height follows
`visualViewport` (`--mx-vvh`). The head script gives the recorded session its scrolling page back
after `motion.shell.fallback` (`data-shell="recorded"`); an element that goes live later takes the
viewport back. The lock lets go whenever the visible height is under 480 CSS px and a keyboard is not
the cause (05): a short window or browser zoom (the layout viewport), or a pinch zoom (`data-zoom` on
the element, set from `visualViewport`). A keyboard shrinks only the visual viewport at scale 1, so it
sets `data-keyboard` instead and the lock holds. With
`interactive-widget=resizes-content` in a page's viewport meta a keyboard would shrink the layout
viewport too; matrix's `Head` does not set it.

What history and the guide's × remember is tab-scoped: `sessionStorage['mx-history']`,
`sessionStorage['mx-guide']`. A stored history that does not parse is an empty one. The Storybook
preview sets `MxTerminal.remember = false`, so a story neither reads nor writes either key (03, 06).

Without scripts: the recorded session, its links real, the status line's and the guide's links plain
links to 人間用. Runs in the output are still buttons (the markup is one), styled as text, and do
nothing.

## Tokens

`color.text-muted`, `color.text-lead`, `color.accent`, `color.panel`, `color.ground`, `color.rule`;
`font.size.ui`, `font.leading.terminal`, `font.weight.medium`; `space.1-5`, `space.3`, `space.4`,
`space.6`; `layer.overlay`.

## Accessibility

The screen is a labelled, focusable group (`Terminal`), so the scrollback scrolls by keyboard; its
outline is drawn inside it. Output is `role="log"` from after the first screen, so arriving does not
read the whole session. Prompts in the scrollback are `aria-hidden`; the commands after them are text.
Japanese runs carry `lang="ja"`. Links in output open a new tab and say so in their name. Keyboard:
Tab reaches the guide's link and ×, the screen, the field, the chips and the status line's link, in
that order. Reduced motion: no blink, an instant change, the rain parked. Forced colours: the cursor
and the status line use system colours.

## Do / Don't

- Do give the element the same interpreter the build used, freshly created.
- Don't print anything a reader typed through anything but `render`.
- Don't put a second terminal on a page.
